input.description: Summarize libghostty-spm wrapper changes
input.prompt:
Repo: https://github.com/Lakr233/libghostty-spm (a Swift Package Manager wrapper around Mitchell Hashimoto's libghostty/Ghostty terminal emulator core, providing Swift bindings + a prebuilt XCFramework). We (a macOS SwiftUI app "Workroom" that embeds terminals) currently pin this dependency at commit df168f41e5a22b319c184e40f021895746ad4e8f, tag "1.2.3" (released 2026-06-01). We want to upgrade to tag "1.3.2" (commit b146b73a8ba3ed2678a22a9de5feecfcbf298d48, released 2026-07-27).

Task: enumerate and summarize every FUNCTIONAL/API change in the wrapper's own Swift layer (not the vendored C libghostty core itself — that's a separate research thread) between commit df168f41e5a22b319c184e40f021895746ad4e8f and tag 1.3.2 (b146b73a). Use the GitHub MCP tools (mcp__plugin_github_github__*, e.g. list_commits, get_commit, compare via get_file_contents diffs, search_commits) — call list_commits with sha=b146b73a8ba3ed2678a22a9de5feecfcbf298d48 and paginate (perPage ~50) until you pass df168f41's commit date (2026-06-01) or you hit df168f41 itself, to get the full commit range. For each merge-PR commit (they're usually "Merge pull request #N from ...") read its message for a one-line description; for the ones that sound functionally significant (new public API, changed method signatures, new options, behavior changes, bug fixes affecting resize/paste/clipboard/surface lifecycle/focus/command execution), fetch the actual diff via get_commit (owner=Lakr233, repo=libghostty-spm, sha=<commit>) to see which files under Sources/ changed and what the change does. Skip pure CI/docs/test-only/version-bump/"chore: autopublish" commits from the detailed summary but you can mention the version bump tags (1.2.4, 1.2.5, ... 1.3.0, 1.3.1, 1.3.2) as version markers.

Known items already spotted (verify and expand, don't just repeat): PR #45 "Expose per-surface command and wait_after_command via TerminalSurfaceOptions" (adds TerminalSurfaceOptions.command: String? and waitAfterCommand: Bool?, marshalled in TerminalController.createSurface); PR #44 "host-managed resize coherence for full-repaint TUIs (opt-in coalescing + pixel-only suppression)"; PR #43 "Add host-managed clipboard confirmation and exec resources" (Talkie project's paste confirmation host callback).

Also check Package.swift / Package.swift.template for any Swift API surface changes (new targets, new min platform versions, new dependencies) between the two refs — diff those two files at df168f41e5a22b319c184e40f021895746ad4e8f vs 1.3.2 using get_file_contents at each ref.

Report format: a chronological bullet list of functional changes (PR title, one-sentence what-changed, which Swift file(s)/API surface affected, and why an app embedding this wrapper might care — e.g. "affects apps that spawn per-surface commands" or "affects apps handling window resize"). End with a short list of any BREAKING changes (signature/behavior changes to existing public API, not just additions). Keep total report under 500 words — this is a research summary, not the full commit log.

input.description: Summarize upstream ghostty core changes
input.prompt:
Repo: https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty — Mitchell Hashimoto's Ghostty terminal emulator, whose core (libghostty) is vendored/built by a separate wrapper we depend on (Lakr233/libghostty-spm). We're upgrading that wrapper, which changes which upstream ghostty commit gets built into our app.

Old pin: upstream ghostty commit 332b2aefc6e72d363aa93ab6ecfc86eeeeb5ed28 (tag v1.3.1, tagged 2026-03-13 by Mitchell Hashimoto).
New pin: upstream ghostty commit 35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58 (untagged, built into wrapper release 1.3.2 on 2026-07-27).

Task: summarize the FUNCTIONAL changes in ghostty-org/ghostty between commit 332b2aefc6e72d363aa93ab6ecfc86eeeeb5ed28 and commit 35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58 — roughly 4.5 months of upstream development, likely hundreds of commits, so you must be selective and focus on what would matter to an embedder using the C API (libghostty) via a Swift wrapper — NOT ghostty's own terminal app UI/config file changes, since we don't use ghostty as a standalone app, only its embeddable surface/terminal core.

Approach: use the GitHub MCP tools (mcp__plugin_github_github__*). Check if any tags exist between v1.3.1 and the 35e1a016 commit (list_tags on ghostty-org/ghostty, or get_tag for v1.3.2/v1.4.0 if they exist) — if 35e1a016 sits after a newer tag, use that tag's release notes (list_releases / get_release_by_tag) as a shortcut summary, since Ghostty publishes real changelogs for its releases (check https://ghostty.org/docs/install/release-notes or a CHANGELOG file in the repo, e.g. path "CHANGELOG.md" at ref 35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58 — try get_file_contents for that). If no changelog file exists, use search_commits or list_commits(sha=35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58) paginated, filtering commit messages/paths for anything touching: src/apprt/embedded* or apprt/*.zig (the embedder API), the surface/Surface.zig, the C API header (include/ghostty.h or src/main_c.zig or similar exported C ABI surface), input handling (keyboard, mouse, focus, DECSET modes like 1004 focus reporting), clipboard/paste, resize/coalescing, shell-integration (OSC 7/9;4/133), font rendering, and anything explicitly changing the public C ABI (new ghostty_* exported functions, changed struct layouts in ghostty_surface_config_s etc). Ignore pure Zig build-system refactors, dependency bumps, typo fixes, and ghostty-app-only features (themes shipped with the standalone app, config file keys) unless they touch the embedder-facing C API too.

Also specifically check: is there a CHANGELOG entry or PR related to DECSET 1004 focus reporting, OSC 9;4 progress reporting, or `ghostty_surface_read_text` / text capture APIs changing between these two commits — we rely on those APIs currently.

Report format: bullet list of functional changes to the embeddable core / C API, each with a one-sentence description and why an embedder (Swift host app driving surfaces) would care, git commit or PR reference. End with an explicit BREAKING CHANGES section (C ABI signature/struct changes) if any were found, or state "no breaking C ABI changes found" if you didn't find any. Keep total report under 500 words.

155	- **Adding/removing/renaming a `.swift` file needs an `xcodegen generate`.** XcodeGen
156	  expands the source glob into explicit file refs in the (gitignored) `.xcodeproj`, so
157	  the change is invisible (or, for a deleted/renamed file, a hard "Build input file
158	  cannot be found" error) until the project is regenerated. The `make app-*` build
159	  targets now run `xcodegen generate` every time, so this is handled automatically —
160	  it only bites when building from Xcode directly (regenerate, or run `make app-generate`).
161	- **SourceKit "Cannot find type X in scope" is usually noise.** The single-file indexer
162	  doesn't see sibling files; a clean `xcodebuild` is authoritative.
163	- **The app binary is also the `ghostty` CLI, and the entry point is `main.swift`, not `@main`.**
164	  `Contents/MacOS/ghostty` is a **relative** symlink to the app binary (a `postCompileScripts` phase
165	  in `project.yml`, before the final code-sign so the link is sealed into the signature).

168	  the action, so calling it alone runs nothing) and exits; otherwise it calls `WorkroomApp.main()`
169	  and the GUI path is byte-for-byte what it was. That branch is why `ghostty_init` was NOT hoisted

173	  (the engine sets `GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR` itself, to the running executable's directory). Side effect:
174	  `ghostty` is on every pane's `PATH` and shadows a real Ghostty.app in there, so a bare `ghostty`

### Evaluate adopting `AppTerminalView` for action-dispatch plumbing (macapp) — reviewed 2026-08-12, not now

**What:** `libghostty-spm` ships more than the raw `GhosttyKit` C-API product we link — a Swift
convenience layer (`Sources/GhosttyTerminal`) with a cross-platform `AppTerminalView`
(AppKit)/`UITerminalView` (UIKit) pair, a `TerminalSurfaceCoordinator`/`TerminalController`, and a
typed delegate family (`TerminalSurfaceTitleDelegate`, `...ResizeDelegate`, `...FocusDelegate`,
`...BellDelegate`, `...ScrollbarDelegate`, `...ProgressReportDelegate`,
`...CommandFinishedDelegate`, `...OpenURLDelegate`, `...HoverLinkDelegate`, `...PwdDelegate`,
`...LifecycleDelegate`, etc.). We use none of it — `GhosttySurfaceView.swift` is our own 2001-line
`NSView` subclass calling `ghostty_surface_config_new()` and the rest of the raw C API directly, with
our own `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter` doing the `GHOSTTY_ACTION_*` switch by hand.

**Checked, not assumed:** `AppTerminalView` is `open class: NSView` (not sealed), and every
input override in `AppTerminalView+Input.swift` (`keyDown`, `mouseDown`, `rightMouseDown`,
`scrollWheel`, `performKeyEquivalent`, …) is itself `override open`, so a subclass in our module
genuinely can override further and call `super`. This is a real, thoughtfully-designed extension
point, not a rebrand of a black box — worth recording so this doesn't get re-litigated on a
surface-level "it's probably sealed" guess.

**Why not now anyway:**
- **It would bundle a UI-layer rewrite with the IO-layer risk the pin bump already carries.**
  Adopting the delegate surface means adopting the coordinator/controller layer underneath it too,
  which is exactly where the packager's `0002-host-managed-io*` patch swap lives (see the pin-bump
  entry above). Evaluating two unknowns — a new engine *and* a new plumbing layer — at once defeats
  the point of bumping the pin first and baking it.
- **Migration cost is real, not mechanical.** `GhosttySurfaceView.swift` encodes ~15-20 documented,
  empirically-discovered AppKit fixes (several **real-mouse-only** — synthetic/XCUITest clicks pass
  on the buggy code, so they can't be regression-tested by CI alone): `.textSelection(.enabled)`
  swallowing real mouseDown, the ⌘-key routing through `AppDelegate`'s monitor rather than
  `event.window`, DECSET-1004 focus reporting via `ghostty_app_set_focus` + window-key handling, the
  backspace-DEL-as-text and ⌃Tab workarounds, mask+contentShape hit-testing during scroll. `open`
  subclassing means each of these is *portable in principle*, but re-deriving exactly where each one
  hooks into `TerminalKeyEventHandler`/`TerminalSurfaceCoordinator` internals we didn't write is
  rediscovery work, not a mechanical port — and several of these fixes have no delegate hook at all
  (they're not events `AppTerminalView` surfaces, they're workarounds for how SwiftUI/AppKit deliver
  events to *any* view underneath them).
- **No pin-bump goal needs it.** `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid`/`ttyName` and
  `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` are both reachable through the raw C API we already call —
  adopting the Swift layer buys nothing for CMT-1/CMT-3.
- **It deepens exactly the coupling CMT-2 (above) is questioning.** Consuming more of a
  single-maintainer package's Swift surface, while a neighboring entry is asking whether to stop
  depending on that same package altogether, is the wrong direction until CMT-2 is resolved.

**What it could buy, if revisited later:** the delegate family plausibly replaces a chunk of
`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter`'s hand-rolled `GHOSTTY_ACTION_*` switch (title/resize/bell/scrollbar/
progress-report/command-finished are all typed callbacks instead of a raw tag switch) — but that's
an argument for adopting the **dispatch layer only**, not for replacing our own input/mouse/keyboard
handling, which is where nearly all the hard-won fixes live.

**Depends on:** the pin bump landing and baking first (see above), and CMT-2's supply-chain question
being settled — no point deepening coupling to a dependency we might drop.

**Priority:** P3 — no feature blocked behind it, reviewed and consciously deferred rather than
unconsidered.

**What:** if/when CMT-2 (above) is actioned, the build mechanics are cheaper than "reuse the
packager's tooling" suggests. `ghostty-org/ghostty`'s own `build.zig` has first-class
`-Demit-xcframework` machinery (`src/build/{Config,XCFrameworkStep,LipoStep,GhosttyXCFramework}.zig`)
— it's what builds `GhosttyKit.xcframework` for **ghostty-org's own** macOS app
(`macos/Ghostty.xcodeproj` links that exact framework). `-Demit-xcframework -Dapp-runtime=none` is
the official surface, confirmed in `Config.zig`'s option defaults; it isn't a reverse-engineered
path, it's the same one ghostty-org's own Mac build uses.

hand-rolled `merge-xcframework.sh` reimplement a slice of that official machinery because their CI
matrix targets 7 slices (macOS × iOS × iOS-sim × Catalyst, for *their* downstream reach — Workroom

universal xcframework directly in one invocation, with no custom lipo script needed.

patches (~200 KB); `0002-host-managed-io*` is load-bearing for embedding, the iOS/Catalyst ones are
not ours to carry. Self-building doesn't remove that decision, it just makes it ours instead of
inherited from Lakr233 — that's the real ongoing cost of CMT-2, not the build mechanics this entry

We link ONLY the raw C-API product (`GhosttyKit`), not that wrapper's Swift convenience classes — we wrote our own `NSView` subclass (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift`, 2001 lines) calling `ghostty_surface_*` C functions directly. Current pin: wrapper package `1.2.3` (commit `df168f41e5a22b319c184e40f021895746ad4e8f`), built from upstream `ghostty-org/ghostty` engine commit `332b2aefc6e72d363aa93ab6ecfc86eeeeb5ed28` (tag `v1.3.1`). Target: wrapper package `1.3.2` (commit `b146b73a8ba3ed2678a22a9de5feecfcbf298d48`), built from ghostty engine commit `35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58` (untagged, ~4 months of upstream commits ahead).

There is an extremely detailed pre-existing TODO entry for this exact bump at `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/TODOS.md` lines 104-232 ("Bump the libghostty pin") — READ IT IN FULL before reviewing anything else; it is the authoritative scoping document and already covers: the package-version-vs-ghostty-version trap, the real risk (a patch swap in the packager's build — `0002-host-managed-io.patch` vs `0002-host-managed-io-modern.patch`, selected by a feature-probe on `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid` presence in the header — affecting PTY/IO hosting, surface teardown, orphan shells), why the `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` enum-renumber is NOT a risk (symbolic dispatch), required blocking work, a rollback plan, and an explicit gate: **this bump is scoped to happen only AFTER the app's GA tag ships — currently the repo is still at `v2.0.0-beta.23`, no GA tag exists.** Also skim `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/TODOS.md` lines 234-310ish (the two follow-on entries "Own the GhosttyKit xcframework" (CMT-2) and "Evaluate adopting AppTerminalView" — both explicitly deferred, not part of this bump).

FRESH RESEARCH DONE THIS SESSION (not yet in TODOS.md, verified via direct GitHub API reads and repo exploration — trust these over guessing):
- Two real breaking upstream C-ABI removals between the two engine commits: `ghostty_app_key_is_binding()` removed (moved to `ghostty_config_key_is_binding`), and the `translated` field removed from `ghostty_input_trigger_u`. Grepped the whole `WorkroomApp*` tree — zero call sites for either. Confirmed zero-risk.
- `ghostty_surface_free_text` was silently NOT freeing memory upstream (header/impl pointer-type mismatch) — now fixed. Our code already calls it correctly at 4 sites in `GhosttySurfaceView.swift` (lines 796, 832, 855, 1630, all via a shared `extractString`/`free_text` pattern) — no code change needed, just a runtime leak sanity-check is worth doing post-bump.
- A crash fix landed upstream: `mouseButtonCallback` raced the I/O thread's scrollback pruning without the renderer mutex on link clicks (use-after-free). Worth a manual regression check: select/click text while scrollback is actively producing output.
- `macapp/QA-libghostty.md` already HAS a "§N Engine bump smoke (run on EVERY libghostty pin change)" section (lines 137-216) with ~19 checkbox items across 4 subsections (IO layer/patch-swap: 7 items; behavior keyed to engine internals incl. "⌘F wrap + ordering": 4 items; resource contract incl. ssh integration: 6 items; build shapes CI doesn't cover: 2 items) — TODOS.md's "Also required" bullet claiming this section "needs to be created" (~12 items) is STALE; it already exists with ~19 items. This should be corrected in TODOS.md as part of this work, not treated as new work.
- The `WorkroomApp.swift:606` EXC_BAD_ACCESS-teardown-comment line reference cited by both TODOS.md and QA-libghostty.md has DRIFTED — the actual comment is now at lines 665-678 (file grew via unrelated commits). Also stale, should be corrected.
- `macapp/project.yml` lines 48-68 hold the pin (`exactVersion: 1.2.3`, unquoted unlike sibling packages) plus a detailed comment block that is explicitly "the single source of truth" for both version numbers (package vs engine) — must be updated in lockstep with the actual bump, not left describing the old pin.
- `Package.resolved` (at `macapp/WorkroomApp.xcodeproj/project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved`) has an `originHash` + schema `version: 3` that SwiftPM/Xcode manages — must be regenerated via Xcode/xcodebuild package resolution, never hand-edited.
- `macapp/Resources/ghostty/SOURCE.md` documents: `terminfo/` is currently BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pinned engine's own terminfo (nothing to regenerate, but MUST re-verify after the bump, not before); `shell-integration/` is currently pinned ~12-52 days AHEAD of the v1.3.1 engine on purpose (carries 4 upstream fixes the old engine's own scripts lack) — since the new engine commit (2026-07-10) is far newer than that window, regenerating shell-integration from the new ref is expected to be a strict upgrade, but should be diffed, not assumed. `GhosttyResourcesTests.swift` (in `WorkroomAppTests/`) enforces: CHECKSUMS covers ONLY terminfo+shell-integration (never themes/, which has its own separate CHECKSUMS/SOURCE.md and must not be touched), no symlinks allowed anywhere in tracked subtrees (a naive `cp -R` from a Ghostty.app tree would reintroduce upstream's `terminfo/67/ghostty` symlink and fail a test — must use `cp -RL` to dereference), and the `terminfo/67/ghostty` alias must stay a byte-identical COPY of `terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty` (not a symlink).

- No automated test anywhere exercises high-volume surface create/destroy churn, the literal `ps`-based orphan-shell-process check, or anything asserting against the documented EXC_BAD_ACCESS teardown race — all of that lives only as manual steps in `QA-libghostty.md` §N today. That's a real, pre-existing gap this bump inherits, not something this bump is expected to fully close.
- `TerminalSearch.swift` lines 70-83 (`navigationPlan`) hard-codes three engine-behavior assumptions (match order is newest→oldest with index 0 = bottom-most; `navigate_search:next` steps newest→oldest so our "Find Next" UI action must emit the engine's `previous` primitive and vice versa; the engine never wraps at the ends, so wrap is synthesized in Swift by emitting `total-1` steps the other way). `TerminalSearchTests.swift` only tests this pure arithmetic with hand-supplied integers — nothing asserts these three assumptions against a live engine round-trip. Whether this needs a code change after the bump is genuinely unknown until manually tested against the new engine (QA-libghostty.md §N already has a checklist item for this, "⌘F wrap + ordering").

MY DRAFT PLAN (review this for gaps, wrong sequencing, missing risks, or over/under-scoping — do NOT just restate it back, actually critique it):

Phase 0 (gate, halts today): verify a GA tag exists (currently doesn't — plan should be ready to fire but not executed past this point until it does).
Phase 1 (mechanical bump): edit project.yml's pin block + comment (lines 48-68) to 1.3.2/35e1a016; regenerate Package.resolved via Xcode package resolution (never hand-edit); clear DerivedData/SourcePackages for a clean resolve.
Phase 2 (resources): clone ghostty-org/ghostty at the new sha; diff terminfo (expect no change, verify don't assume); regenerate shell-integration via `cp -RL` (dereference); regenerate CHECKSUMS (terminfo+shell-integration only); update SOURCE.md's provenance/pin tables; run GhosttyResourcesTests locally.
Phase 3 (new tests): add a `+ssh --help` exit-0 dispatch test to GhosttyCLITests.swift mirroring the existing +ssh-cache pattern; flag (don't yet solve) that TODOS.md also wants a REAL end-to-end SSH-through-the-wrapper test, which needs a reachable test host/sshd and needs its own small feasibility spike before committing to an approach.
Phase 4 (IO-layer + search verification, manual): run QA-libghostty.md §N in full (all ~19 existing items) as the actual regression gate since no automated coverage exists for surface churn/orphan-check/EXC_BAD_ACCESS; add two new checklist items to §N's IO-layer subsection (select/click during active scrollback output; a free_text leak spot-check loop); resolve TerminalSearch.navigationPlan conditionally — only touch the code if the existing "⌘F wrap + ordering" manual check reveals an actual behavior change.
Phase 5 (explicitly out of scope): do NOT wire ghostty_surface_foreground_pid/ttyName or GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED in this same change — just confirm the build compiles cleanly against the new header.
Phase 6 (release gates): local universal build sanity check (`VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal make app-vcs` + Release xcodebuild), then land on master and let nightly.yml's existing daily make app-test → make app-release cycle be the bake gate; keep the backspace-DEL-as-text and ⌃Tab workarounds until baked.
Phase 7 (rollback): revert + rm -rf DerivedData/SourcePackages + rebuild; bust CI's spm-/xcbuild- caches too since they key on project.yml.
Phase 8 (doc hygiene, cheap, do alongside): fix the two stale line-references (WorkroomApp.swift:606→665-678) and correct TODOS.md's claim that QA-libghostty.md §N needs to be created (it already exists) in both TODOS.md and QA-libghostty.md.

Critique this plan. Specifically: (1) is the phase ordering right, or should something happen earlier/later (e.g. should resource regen happen before or after the SPM pin bump; should doc hygiene be its own commit vs bundled); (2) is anything load-bearing missing that TODOS.md or the fresh research implies but my draft doesn't capture; (3) is Phase 3's "real SSH test" framing (flag-not-solve) the right call given repo conventions, or is there an existing pattern elsewhere in this codebase for spinning up a local test service (loopback sshd, docker, expect-script) I should point to instead of treating it as unknown; (4) should this be one commit or several (e.g. separate the doc-hygiene fixes from the actual bump); (5) anything in the "explicitly out of scope" phase that's actually wrong to defer. Keep the response to actionable critique only, under 600 words — this is a review, not a rewrite.

# Bump the libghostty pin (1.2.3 → 1.3.2)

## Context

Workroom's terminal is `GhosttyKit.xcframework`, distributed by third-party wrapper
`Lakr233/libghostty-spm` and pinned exactly in `macapp/project.yml` (the embedding C API isn't
stable, so no floating version). We link only the raw `GhosttyKit` C-API product — our own
`GhosttySurfaceView.swift` (2001 lines) drives `ghostty_surface_*` directly; we don't consume the
wrapper's Swift convenience layer.

Current pin: wrapper `1.2.3` (`df168f41`), built from upstream `ghostty-org/ghostty` engine
`332b2aef` (tag `v1.3.1`, 2026-03-13). Target: wrapper `1.3.2` (`b146b73a`), built from engine
`35e1a016` (untagged, 2026-07-10) — roughly four months and ~1300 commits of upstream fixes,
including two capabilities nothing else can reach: `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid`/`tty_name`
(blocked: CMT-1, "no PTY child PID") and `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` (an optimization path
for CMT-3's a11y hook, already shipped 2026-08-10 via a 400ms poll workaround).

This bump is fully scoped already at `TODOS.md:104-232` ("Bump the libghostty pin") — that entry,
plus fresh research done this session (verified against actual source, not assumed), is the basis
for this plan. Two related decisions it surfaces (owning the xcframework build; adopting the
wrapper's `AppTerminalView` convenience layer) are filed as separate, deliberately-deferred TODOS.md
entries and are **not** part of this plan.

**Hard gate — this plan does not execute past Phase 0 today.** `TODOS.md` scopes this as
"post-GA, first change after the GA tag." The repo is currently at `v2.0.0-beta.24`; no `v2.0.0`
tag exists. Phase 0 checks for that tag specifically (not any non-prerelease tag — `v1.0.0`
through `v1.3.0` already exist as unrelated pre-rewrite releases) and halts if absent.

## What's corrected vs. what TODOS.md currently says

- `QA-libghostty.md` already has a full "§N Engine bump smoke" section (`QA-libghostty.md:137-216`,
  4 subsections) — TODOS.md's "Also required" bullet claiming it "needs to be created" is stale.
  Its own preamble also states the baseline must be run **before** the bump, not after — the current
  plan phasing (below) respects that.
- `WorkroomApp.swift:606` (cited by both TODOS.md and QA-libghostty.md for the EXC_BAD_ACCESS
  teardown comment) has drifted — the actual comment is now at `WorkroomApp.swift:665-678`.
- Two upstream fixes not yet in either doc: `ghostty_surface_free_text` was silently not freeing
  memory (now fixed — our 4 call sites in `GhosttySurfaceView.swift` need no code change, just a
  leak sanity-check); a `mouseButtonCallback`/scrollback-pruning race (use-after-free on link
  clicks) is fixed — worth a targeted regression check.
- Two real C-ABI removals upstream (`ghostty_app_key_is_binding`, `ghostty_input_trigger_u.translated`)
  — grepped the whole app, zero call sites for either. Zero risk, no action needed.
- The CI xcbuild cache (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has no `restore-keys` fallback — only the SPM
  cache does. A revert only needs to worry about the SPM cache carrying stale state.

## Phase 1 — Pre-bump baseline (before touching anything)

Run `QA-libghostty.md` §N in full against the **current** engine and record results — its own
preamble requires this, since several items only have a "same as before" pass criterion. Also run
the `SelectionGesture` drag/click-threshold check (TODOS.md:170) even though it's not in §N today,
since the upstream rewrite touches exactly that path.

Add two new checklist items to §N's "IO layer" subsection now, and baseline them too:
- Select/click text while scrollback is actively producing output (regression target for the
  `mouseButtonCallback` race fix).

  (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:792-857`) a few hundred times, watch RSS for unbounded growth.

  (it's the documented single source of truth) to state package `1.3.2` / engine `35e1a016`.

  via Xcode/`xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies` after `make app-generate` — never hand-edit;
  it carries an `originHash` SwiftPM manages.

- Build once and confirm the modulemap-collision workaround (`macapp/CLAUDE.md:120-124`, "Multiple
  commands produce include/module.modulemap") still holds under the new xcframework's header layout
  — a build failure here surfaces immediately, no separate step needed to detect it.
- Confirm the build compiles clean against the new header. Do **not** wire
  `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid`/`tty_name` or a `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` case in
  `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.handleAction` (`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift:25-141`) — both are separate,
  already-tracked follow-ups (CMT-1, CMT-3-optimization), not part of this bump. The new action tag
  falling into the existing `default:` arm (logs once in Debug) is expected and fine.

## Phase 3 — Resource regeneration

- Clone `ghostty-org/ghostty` at `35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58`.
- `terminfo/`: per `Resources/ghostty/SOURCE.md:30-43` this is currently byte-identical to the
  engine's own — diff against the new checkout to confirm still true; do not blindly regenerate.
- `shell-integration/`: copy with `cp -RL` (dereference — `GhosttyResourcesTests` hard-fails on any
  symlink in a tracked subtree). Current scripts are pinned ~12-52 days ahead of the *old* engine on
  purpose (SOURCE.md:45-71); since the new engine commit is from 2026-07-10, regenerating is expected
  to be a strict upgrade — diff to confirm none of the 4 documented upstream fixes regress.
- Keep `terminfo/67/ghostty` a byte-identical **copy** of `terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty` (not upstream's
  symlink) — required by `GhosttyResourcesTests.testTerminfoAliasMatchesPrimaryEntry`.
- Regenerate `Resources/ghostty/CHECKSUMS` (`shasum -a 256`, terminfo + shell-integration only —
  never `themes/`, which has its own separate `CHECKSUMS`/`SOURCE.md` and must not be touched).
- Update `SOURCE.md`: refresh the Provenance "measured against" pin, the shell-integration
  blob-hash/commit-range table, and resolve the ssh-wrapper section now that `+ssh` genuinely exists
  at this pin (it doesn't at v1.3.1).
- Run `GhosttyResourcesTests` locally — all four assertions (checksum match both directions, no
  unexpected top-level entries, themes excluded, alias byte-identical) must pass.

## Phase 4 — SSH: dispatch test now, real-host spike as its own step

- Add a dispatch test to `GhosttyCLITests.swift` (mirrors `testGhosttyRunsSshCacheActionAndWritesCache`
  at line 91): run `["+ssh", "--help"]` via the existing `runGhostty` helper, assert exit 0 — this
  matches TODOS.md's explicit spec ("asserted the way `release.sh` already asserts `+ssh-cache`",
  confirmed at `release.sh:212-216` to be exit-code-based) — and additionally assert stdout contains
  expected help text where cheap, consistent with how `testGhosttyRejectsInvalidAction` goes beyond
  a bare exit code.
- Per your call: spike a local loopback `sshd` (macOS ships `/usr/sbin/sshd`) on `127.0.0.1` at an
  ephemeral port, driven the same way `GhosttyCLITests` already drives processes
  (`Process()` + `addTeardownBlock`, lines 36-62). Goal: actually `ssh` through the regenerated
  wrapper script end-to-end. If it runs cleanly and isn't flaky in CI (no TCC/Remote-Login prompts,
  no port conflicts), land it as an automated test alongside the dispatch test above. If it proves
  unreliable in CI (sandboxing, permissions), fall back to the existing manual QA step
  (`QA-libghostty.md:187-199`, "ssh integration" — already explicitly scoped as "the part that needs
  a real remote host") rather than shipping a flaky test.

## Phase 5 — Post-bump retest (the actual regression gate)

No automated test today covers high-volume surface churn, the literal `ps` orphan-shell check, or
anything asserting the EXC_BAD_ACCESS teardown race (`WorkroomApp.swift:665-678`) — confirmed by
direct search. This remains a manual gate:

- Re-run `QA-libghostty.md` §N in full against the new engine and diff against the Phase 1 baseline —
  including the two new IO-layer items and the `SelectionGesture` check added in Phase 1.
- Name the automated half of the gate explicitly rather than leaving it implicit: TODOS.md's
  "XCUITest action-tag baseline" is `GhosttyActionDispatchUITests.testRunningCommandRetitlesTheTabChip`
  and `testOSCProgressReportMarksTheTabBusyThenIdle` (lines 97, 118) — run these against the new
  engine as the automated pass/fail complement to §N.
- `TerminalSearch.navigationPlan` (`TerminalSearch.swift:70-83`): touch this **only if** §N's
  "⌘F wrap + ordering" item reveals actual behavior change (direction, wrap point, or match-order
  semantics). If unchanged, no code or test edit needed — record that it was checked.

## Phase 6 — Release gates (mostly already-existing machinery, not new work)

- Local sanity check before pushing (optional signal): `VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal make app-vcs`,
  then `xcodebuild -configuration Release ARCHS="arm64 x86_64" ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=NO build`.
- Land on `master`. `nightly.yml` already runs `make app-test` (gate) → `make app-release`
  (universal, notarized) daily — this is the bake gate. Decide how many clean nightlies to require
  before promoting to a `pre` tag (not specified anywhere today — your call at that point).
- Do not remove the backspace-DEL-as-text (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:1171`) or ⌃Tab workarounds
  until baked — both fail safe either way, so removal needs its own raw-PTY probe, not this bump.

## Rollback

Revert the commit(s), `rm -rf macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages`, rebuild. Only the CI **SPM** cache
(`ci.yml`, `restore-keys: spm-${os}-`) risks restoring stale state on a revert — the xcbuild cache
has no restore-keys fallback, so a revert is just a clean cache miss there, nothing to bust.

## Commits

1. **Doc hygiene first, standalone** (land before the bump so whoever reads TODOS.md next sees
   correct state): fix the two stale line references (`WorkroomApp.swift:606` → `665-678`) in both
   `TODOS.md` and `QA-libghostty.md`, and correct TODOS.md's "§N needs to be created" claim.
2. **The bump itself, one commit** (Phases 2-4 — TODOS.md itself frames pin + resources + ssh tests
   as "same commit"): `project.yml`, `Package.resolved`, `Resources/ghostty/*`, `GhosttyCLITests.swift`
   (+ the sshd spike test if it lands).
3. Phase 1 (baseline) and Phase 5 (retest) are manual QA passes, not commits — their only artifact
   is the recorded §N results and the checklist additions from Phase 1 (which land as part of commit 1
   or 2, whichever is more convenient at execution time).

## Verification

- `make app-test` green, including `GhosttyResourcesTests` (all 4 assertions) and the new
  `GhosttyCLITests` `+ssh --help` dispatch test.
- `QA-libghostty.md` §N fully re-run against the new engine, diffed against the Phase 1 baseline —
  this is the actual regression gate for the patch-swap risk; nothing else exercises it.
- `GhosttyActionDispatchUITests`'s two named tests pass against the new engine.
- If the sshd spike lands: its test passes reliably (run it a few times locally, not just once —
  loopback network tests are the class of thing that flakes under CI resource contention).
- Universal Release build links (`lipo -info` shows both slices) — either via the local sanity
  check or by trusting `nightly.yml`'s daily run.

1. **Auto-decide denial (NOT a failure).** The result contains `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` — the preference hook working as designed. Proceed with that option. Do NOT retry, do NOT fall back to prose.
2. **Genuine failure** — no variant in your tool list, OR the variant is present but the call returns an error / missing result (MCP transport error, empty result, host bug — e.g. Conductor's MCP AskUserQuestion is flaky and returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`).

Split chains / 5+ options: one prose block per per-option call, in sequence. Then STOP and wait — the user's typed answer is the decision. In plan mode this satisfies end-of-turn like a tool call.

**Continuation — mapping a typed reply back to a brief.** Each brief carries a stable label (`D<N>`, or `D<N>.k` in a split chain). The user references it (e.g. "3.2: B"). A bare letter maps to the single most-recent UNANSWERED brief; if more than one is open (a split chain), do NOT guess — ask which `D<N>.k` it answers. Never apply a bare letter ambiguously across a chain.

**One-way / destructive confirmations in prose.** When the decision is a one-way door (irreversible or destructive — delete, force-push, drop, overwrite), prose is a WEAKER gate than the tool, so make it stronger: require an explicit typed confirmation (the exact option letter or word), state plainly what is irreversible, and NEVER proceed on a vague, partial, or ambiguous reply — re-ask instead. Treat silence or "ok"/"sure" without the explicit choice as not-yet-confirmed.

### Format

Every AskUserQuestion is a decision brief and must be sent as tool_use, not prose — unless the documented failure fallback above applies (interactive session + the call is unavailable/erroring), in which case the prose fallback is the correct output.

```
D<N> — <one-line question title>
Project/branch/task: <1 short grounding sentence using _BRANCH>
ELI10: <plain English a 16-year-old could follow, 2-4 sentences, name the stakes>
Stakes if we pick wrong: <one sentence on what breaks, what user sees, what's lost>
Recommendation: <choice> because <one-line reason>
Completeness: A=X/10, B=Y/10   (or: Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score)
Pros / cons:
A) <option label> (recommended)
  ✅ <pro — concrete, observable, ≥40 chars>
  ❌ <con — honest, ≥40 chars>
B) <option label>
  ✅ <pro>
  ❌ <con>
Net: <one-line synthesis of what you're actually trading off>
```

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Pros / cons: use ✅ and ❌. Minimum 2 pros and 1 con per option when the choice is real; Minimum 40 characters per bullet. Hard-stop escape for one-way/destructive confirmations: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

Net line closes the tradeoff. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit. Pick a compliant shape:

- **Batch into ≤4-groups** — for coherent alternatives (e.g. version bumps,
  layout variants). One call, 5th surfaced only if first 4 don't fit.
- **Split per-option** — for independent scope items (e.g. "ship E1..E6?").
  Fire N sequential calls, one per option. Default to this when unsure.

Per-option call shape: `D<N>.k` header (e.g. D3.1..D3.5), ELI10 per option,
Recommendation, kind-note (no completeness score — Include/Defer/Cut/Hold are
decision actions), and 4 buckets:
**A) Include**, **B) Defer**, **C) Cut**, **D) Hold** (stop chain, discuss).

After the chain, fire `D<N>.final` to validate the assembled set (reprompt
dependency conflicts) and confirm shipping it. Use `D<N>.revise-<k>` to
revise one option without re-running the chain.

For N>6, fire a `D<N>.0` meta-AskUserQuestion first (proceed / narrow / batch).

question_ids for split chains: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>` (kebab-case ASCII,
≤64 chars, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision). The runtime checker
(`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on any `*-split-*` id,
so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible — the user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:** see
`docs/askuserquestion-split.md` in the gstack repo. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** When any string
field contains Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or other non-ASCII text,
emit the literal UTF-8 characters; never escape them as `\uXXXX` (the pipe is
UTF-8 native, and manual escaping miscodes long CJK strings). Only `\n`,
`\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale + worked example: see
`docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`. Read on demand when a question contains CJK.

### Self-check before emitting

Before calling AskUserQuestion, verify:
- [ ] D<N> header present
- [ ] ELI10 paragraph present (stakes line too)
- [ ] Recommendation line present with concrete reason
- [ ] Completeness scored (coverage) OR kind-note present (kind)
- [ ] Every option has ≥2 ✅ and ≥1 ❌, each ≥40 chars (or hard-stop escape)
- [ ] (recommended) label on one option (even for neutral-posture)
- [ ] Dual-scale effort labels on effort-bearing options (human / CC)
- [ ] Net line closes the decision
- [ ] You are calling the tool, not writing prose — unless `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` (then prose is the DEFAULT, not the tool) OR the documented failure fallback applies (then: prose with the mandatory triad — issue ELI10, per-choice Completeness, Recommendation + `(recommended)` — and a "reply with a letter" instruction, then STOP)
- [ ] Non-ASCII characters (CJK / accents) written directly, NOT \u-escaped
- [ ] If you had 5+ options, you split (or batched into ≤4-groups) — did NOT drop any
- [ ] If you split, you checked dependencies between options before firing the chain
- [ ] If a per-option Hold fires, you stopped the chain immediately (didn't queue)

```bash

# Prefer the v1.27.0.0 artifacts file; fall back to brain file for users

# Per-worktree pin: post-spike redesign uses kubectl-style `.gbrain-source` in the
# git toplevel to scope queries. Look for the pin in the worktree (not a global
# state file) so that opening worktree B without a pin doesn't claim "indexed"
# just because worktree A was synced. Empty string when gbrain is not
# configured (zero context cost for non-gbrain users).
_GBRAIN_CONFIG="$HOME/.gbrain/config.json"
if [ -f "$_GBRAIN_CONFIG" ] && command -v gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  _GBRAIN_VERSION_OK=$(gbrain --version 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^gbrain ' || echo 0)
  if [ "$_GBRAIN_VERSION_OK" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH=""
    _REPO_TOP=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ -n "$_REPO_TOP" ] && [ -f "$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source" ]; then
      _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH="$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source"
    fi
    if [ -n "$_GBRAIN_PIN_PATH" ]; then
      echo "GBrain configured. Prefer \`gbrain search\`/\`gbrain query\` over Grep for"
      echo "semantic questions; use \`gbrain code-def\`/\`code-refs\`/\`code-callers\` for"
      echo "symbol-aware code lookup. See \"## GBrain Search Guidance\" in CLAUDE.md."
      echo "Run /sync-gbrain to refresh."
    else
      echo "GBrain configured but this worktree isn't pinned yet. Run \`/sync-gbrain --full\`"
      echo "before relying on \`gbrain search\` for code questions in this worktree."
      echo "Falls back to Grep until pinned."
    fi
  fi
fi

_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE=$("$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN" get artifacts_sync_mode 2>/dev/null || echo off)

# Detect remote-MCP mode (Path 4 of /setup-gbrain). Local artifacts sync is
# a no-op in remote mode; the brain server pulls from GitHub/GitLab on its
# own cadence. Read claude.json directly to keep this preamble fast (no
# subprocess to claude CLI on every skill start).
_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="none"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$HOME/.claude.json" ]; then
  _GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.type // .mcpServers.gbrain.transport // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$_GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE" in
    url|http|sse) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="remote-http" ;;
    stdio) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="local-stdio" ;;
  esac
fi

if [ -f "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" ] && [ ! -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" = "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_NEW_URL=$(head -1 "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
  if [ -n "$_BRAIN_NEW_URL" ]; then
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: artifacts repo detected: $_BRAIN_NEW_URL"
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: run 'gstack-brain-restore' to pull your cross-machine artifacts (or 'gstack-config set artifacts_sync_mode off' to dismiss forever)"
  fi
fi

if [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE="$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-pull"
  _BRAIN_NOW=$(date +%s)
  _BRAIN_DO_PULL=1
  if [ -f "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" ]; then
    _BRAIN_LAST=$(cat "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    _BRAIN_AGE=$(( _BRAIN_NOW - _BRAIN_LAST ))
    [ "$_BRAIN_AGE" -lt 86400 ] && _BRAIN_DO_PULL=0
  fi
  if [ "$_BRAIN_DO_PULL" = "1" ]; then
    ( cd "$_GSTACK_HOME" && git fetch origin >/dev/null 2>&1 && git merge --ff-only "origin/$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" >/dev/null 2>&1 ) || true
    echo "$_BRAIN_NOW" > "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE"
  fi

fi

if [ "$_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE" = "remote-http" ]; then
  # Remote-MCP mode: local artifacts sync is a no-op (brain admin's server
  # pulls from GitHub/GitLab). Show the user this is by design, not broken.
  _GBRAIN_HOST=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.url // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's|^https?://([^/:]+).*|\1|')
  echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: remote-mode (managed by brain server ${_GBRAIN_HOST:-remote})"
elif [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH=0
  [ -f "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-queue.jsonl" ] && _BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH=$(wc -l < "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-queue.jsonl" | tr -d ' ')

else

fi
```

## Model-Specific Behavioral Patch (claude)

The following nudges are tuned for the claude model family. They are
**subordinate** to skill workflow, STOP points, AskUserQuestion gates, plan-mode
safety, and /ship review gates. If a nudge below conflicts with skill instructions,
the skill wins. Treat these as preferences, not rules.

**Todo-list discipline.** When working through a multi-step plan, mark each task
complete individually as you finish it. Do not batch-complete at the end. If a task
turns out to be unnecessary, mark it skipped with a one-line reason.

**Think before heavy actions.** For complex operations (refactors, migrations,
non-trivial new features), briefly state your approach before executing. This lets
the user course-correct cheaply instead of mid-flight.

**Dedicated tools over Bash.** Prefer Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep over shell
equivalents (cat, sed, find, grep). The dedicated tools are cheaper and clearer.

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment, compressed for runtime.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.
- Be concrete. Name files, functions, line numbers, commands, outputs, evals, and real numbers.
- Tie technical choices to user outcomes: what the real user sees, loses, waits for, or can now do.
- Be direct about quality. Bugs matter. Edge cases matter. Fix the whole thing, not the demo path.
- Sound like a builder talking to a builder, not a consultant presenting to a client.
- Never corporate, academic, PR, or hype. Avoid filler, throat-clearing, generic optimism, and founder cosplay.
- No em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive, nuanced, multifaceted, furthermore, moreover, additionally, pivotal, landscape, tapestry, underscore, foster, showcase, intricate, vibrant, fundamental, significant.
- The user has context you do not: domain knowledge, timing, relationships, taste. Cross-model agreement is a recommendation, not a decision. The user decides.

Good: "auth.ts:47 returns undefined when the session cookie expires. Users hit a white screen. Fix: add a null check and redirect to /login. Two lines."
Bad: "I've identified a potential issue in the authentication flow that may cause problems under certain conditions."

## Writing Style (skip entirely if `EXPLAIN_LEVEL: terse` appears in the preamble echo OR the user's current message explicitly requests terse / no-explanations output)

Applies to AskUserQuestion, user replies, and findings. AskUserQuestion Format is structure; this is prose quality.

- Gloss curated jargon on first use per skill invocation, even if the user pasted the term.
- Frame questions in outcome terms: what pain is avoided, what capability unlocks, what user experience changes.
- Use short sentences, concrete nouns, active voice.
- Close decisions with user impact: what the user sees, waits for, loses, or gains.
- User-turn override wins: if the current message asks for terse / no explanations / just the answer, skip this section.
- Terse mode (EXPLAIN_LEVEL: terse): no glosses, no outcome-framing layer, shorter responses.

Curated jargon list lives at `~/.claude/skills/gstack/scripts/jargon-list.json` (80+ terms). On the first jargon term you encounter this session, Read that file once; treat the `terms` array as the canonical list. The list is repo-owned and may grow between releases.


## Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean

AI makes completeness cheap, so the complete thing is the goal. Recommend full coverage (tests, edge cases, error paths) — boil the ocean one lake at a time. The only thing out of scope is genuinely unrelated work (rewrites, multi-quarter migrations); flag that as separate scope, never as an excuse for a shortcut.

When options differ in coverage, include `Completeness: X/10` (10 = all edge cases, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut). When options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.` Do not fabricate scores.

## Confusion Protocol

For high-stakes ambiguity (architecture, data model, destructive scope, missing context), STOP. Name it in one sentence, present 2-3 options with tradeoffs, and ask. Do not use for routine coding or obvious changes.

## Continuous Checkpoint Mode

If `CHECKPOINT_MODE` is `"continuous"`: auto-commit completed logical units with `WIP:` prefix.

Commit after new intentional files, completed functions/modules, verified bug fixes, and before long-running install/build/test commands.

Commit format:

```
WIP: <concise description of what changed>

[gstack-context]
Decisions: <key choices made this step>
Remaining: <what's left in the logical unit>
Tried: <failed approaches worth recording> (omit if none)
Skill: </skill-name-if-running>
[/gstack-context]
```

Rules: stage only intentional files, NEVER `git add -A`, do not commit broken tests or mid-edit state, and push only if `CHECKPOINT_PUSH` is `"true"`. Do not announce each WIP commit.

`/context-restore` reads `[gstack-context]`; `/ship` squashes WIP commits into clean commits.

If `CHECKPOINT_MODE` is `"explicit"`: ignore this section unless a skill or user asks to commit.

If you are looping on the same diagnostic, same file, or failed fix variants, STOP and reassess. Consider escalation or /context-save. Progress summaries must NEVER mutate git state.

## Question Tuning (skip entirely if `QUESTION_TUNING: false`)

Before each AskUserQuestion, choose `question_id` from `scripts/question-registry.ts` or `{skill}-{slug}`, then run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-question-preference --check "<id>"`. `AUTO_DECIDE` means choose the recommended option and say "Auto-decided [summary] → [option] (your preference). Change with /plan-tune." `ASK_NORMALLY` means ask.

**Embed the question_id as a marker in the question text** so hooks can identify it deterministically (plan-tune cathedral T14 / D18 progressive markers). Append `<gstack-qid:{question_id}>` somewhere in the rendered question (the leading line or trailing line is fine; the marker doesn't render visibly to the user when wrapped in HTML-style angle brackets, but the hook strips it). Without the marker the PreToolUse enforcement hook treats the AUQ as observed-only and never auto-decides — so always include it when the question matches a registered `question_id`.

**Embed the option recommendation via the `(recommended)` label suffix** on exactly one option per AUQ. The PreToolUse hook parses `(recommended)` first, falls back to "Recommendation: X" prose, and refuses to auto-decide if ambiguous. Two `(recommended)` labels = refuse.

Skills that run plan reviews (`/plan-*-review`, `/codex review`) include the EXIT PLAN MODE GATE blocking checklist at the end of the skill, which verifies the plan file ends with `## GSTACK REVIEW REPORT` before ExitPlanMode is called. # Plan Review Mode

Review this plan thoroughly before making any code changes. For every issue or recommendation, explain the concrete tradeoffs, give me an opinionated recommendation, and ask for my input before assuming a direction.

## Scope gate (FIRST — overrides everything below). This is a hard STOP.

Before ANYTHING else in this skill — before the Design Doc Check, the office-hours prerequisite offer, Step 0, and any `git` / `Read` / `Grep` / `Glob` / `Bash` call — your VERY FIRST tool call MUST be AskUserQuestion, to confirm the review target. Do not run the Design Doc Check bash or explore the repo before the user answers.

1. First tool call = AskUserQuestion (tool_use). Confirm what to review.
2. Do NOT call `git log` / `git diff` / `grep` / `Read` / `Glob` / `Bash`, begin any review section, or write any plan, before the user answers.
3. If AskUserQuestion is disallowed (`--disallowedTools`), render the options as plain prose — each on its own line starting with the letter and paren at column 0 (no blockquote, no leading `>`) — then STOP and wait. Use exactly this shape:

What should I review?
A) The current branch diff — the work in progress on this branch.
B) A plan or design doc I'll paste or point you to.
C) A specific file, directory, or path.

Recommendation: A when a branch diff exists, otherwise B. Reply with A, B, or C. STOP and wait for the answer — only after the user picks do you run the Design Doc Check and Step 0 against that target.

## Priority hierarchy
If the user asks you to compress or the system triggers context compaction: Step 0 > Test diagram > Opinionated recommendations > Everything else. Never skip Step 0 or the test diagram. Do not preemptively warn about context limits -- the system handles compaction automatically.

## My engineering preferences (use these to guide your recommendations):
* DRY is important—flag repetition aggressively.
* Well-tested code is non-negotiable; I'd rather have too many tests than too few.
* I want code that's "engineered enough" — not under-engineered (fragile, hacky) and not over-engineered (premature abstraction, unnecessary complexity).
* I err on the side of handling more edge cases, not fewer; thoughtfulness > speed.
* Bias toward explicit over clever.
* Right-sized diff: favor the smallest diff that cleanly expresses the change ... but don't compress a necessary rewrite into a minimal patch. If the existing foundation is broken, say "scrap it and do this instead."

## Cognitive Patterns — How Great Eng Managers Think

These are not additional checklist items. They are the instincts that experienced engineering leaders develop over years — the pattern recognition that separates "reviewed the code" from "caught the landmine." Apply them throughout your review.

1. **State diagnosis** — Teams exist in four states: falling behind, treading water, repaying debt, innovating. Each demands a different intervention (Larson, An Elegant Puzzle).
2. **Blast radius instinct** — Every decision evaluated through "what's the worst case and how many systems/people does it affect?"
3. **Boring by default** — "Every company gets about three innovation tokens." Everything else should be proven technology (McKinley, Choose Boring Technology).
4. **Incremental over revolutionary** — Strangler fig, not big bang. Canary, not global rollout. Refactor, not rewrite (Fowler).
5. **Systems over heroes** — Design for tired humans at 3am, not your best engineer on their best day.
6. **Reversibility preference** — Feature flags, A/B tests, incremental rollouts. Make the cost of being wrong low.
7. **Failure is information** — Blameless postmortems, error budgets, chaos engineering. Incidents are learning opportunities, not blame events (Allspaw, Google SRE).
8. **Org structure IS architecture** — Conway's Law in practice. Design both intentionally (Skelton/Pais, Team Topologies).
9. **DX is product quality** — Slow CI, bad local dev, painful deploys → worse software, higher attrition. Developer experience is a leading indicator.
10. **Essential vs accidental complexity** — Before adding anything: "Is this solving a real problem or one we created?" (Brooks, No Silver Bullet).
11. **Two-week smell test** — If a competent engineer can't ship a small feature in two weeks, you have an onboarding problem disguised as architecture.
12. **Glue work awareness** — Recognize invisible coordination work. Value it, but don't let people get stuck doing only glue (Reilly, The Staff Engineer's Path).
13. **Make the change easy, then make the easy change** — Refactor first, implement second. Never structural + behavioral changes simultaneously (Beck).
14. **Own your code in production** — No wall between dev and ops. "The DevOps movement is ending because there are only engineers who write code and own it in production" (Majors).
15. **Error budgets over uptime targets** — SLO of 99.9% = 0.1% downtime *budget to spend on shipping*. Reliability is resource allocation (Google SRE).

When evaluating architecture, think "boring by default." When reviewing tests, think "systems over heroes." When assessing complexity, ask Brooks's question. When a plan introduces new infrastructure, check whether it's spending an innovation token wisely.

## Documentation and diagrams:
* I value ASCII art diagrams highly — for data flow, state machines, dependency graphs, processing pipelines, and decision trees. Use them liberally in plans and design docs.
* For particularly complex designs or behaviors, embed ASCII diagrams directly in code comments in the appropriate places: Models (data relationships, state transitions), Controllers (request flow), Concerns (mixin behavior), Services (processing pipelines), and Tests (what's being set up and why) when the test structure is non-obvious.
* **Diagram maintenance is part of the change.** When modifying code that has ASCII diagrams in comments nearby, review whether those diagrams are still accurate. Update them as part of the same commit. Stale diagrams are worse than no diagrams — they actively mislead. Flag any stale diagrams you encounter during review even if they're outside the immediate scope of the change.

### Step 0: Scope Challenge

> Reminder: the **Scope gate** at the top of this skill is a hard STOP. Do not run Step 0 until the user has answered it, and run it against the target they chose.

Before reviewing anything, answer these questions:
1. **What existing code already partially or fully solves each sub-problem?** Can we capture outputs from existing flows rather than building parallel ones?
2. **What is the minimum set of changes that achieves the stated goal?** Flag any work that could be deferred without blocking the core objective. Be ruthless about scope creep.
3. **Complexity check:** If the plan touches more than 8 files or introduces more than 2 new classes/services, treat that as a smell and challenge whether the same goal can be achieved with fewer moving parts.
4. **Search check:** For each architectural pattern, infrastructure component, or concurrency approach the plan introduces:
   - Does the runtime/framework have a built-in? Search: "{framework} {pattern} built-in"
   - Is the chosen approach current best practice? Search: "{pattern} best practice {current year}"
   - Are there known footguns? Search: "{framework} {pattern} pitfalls"

   If WebSearch is unavailable, skip this check and note: "Search unavailable — proceeding with in-distribution knowledge only."

5. **TODOS cross-reference:** Read `TODOS.md` if it exists. Are any deferred items blocking this plan? Can any deferred items be bundled into this PR without expanding scope? Does this plan create new work that should be captured as a TODO?

5. **Completeness check:** Is the plan doing the complete version or a shortcut? With AI-assisted coding, the cost of completeness (100% test coverage, full edge case handling, complete error paths) is 10-100x cheaper than with a human team. If the plan proposes a shortcut that saves human-hours but only saves minutes with CC+gstack, recommend the complete version. Boil the ocean.

6. **Distribution check:** If the plan introduces a new artifact type (CLI binary, library package, container image, mobile app), does it include the build/publish pipeline? Code without distribution is code nobody can use. Check:

1 — Architecture: the entire regression gate for this bump's real risk (the host-managed-io patch swap — PTY/IO hosting, surface teardown, orphan shells) is a manual QA-libghostty.md checklist. Nothing automated asserts against the EXC_BAD_ACCESS teardown race, the literal `ps` orphan-shell check, or high-volume surface churn — confirmed zero hits across every test file this session. One missed checklist item on a future bump ships a broken IO patch straight to users with silent orphaned shells.
ELI10: The scariest part of swapping the terminal engine — does it clean up child processes correctly when panes close or the app quits — is currently checked by a human reading a markdown checklist, not by any test that runs itself.
Stakes if we pick wrong: leave it manual and someone eventually skips a step under release pressure — or invest engineering time now on a bump that's already gated behind a GA tag that hasn't shipped yet, delaying a low-risk-otherwise change.
Recommendation: 1C — file it as its own follow-up TODO rather than build new XCUITest process-assertion infra (something no existing UI test does) inside this already-narrowly-scoped bump.
Completeness: 1A=3/10, 1B=9/10, 1C=6/10 (acknowledges the gap without solving it, closer to complete than doing nothing).

questions.question:
4 — Performance: Phase 1's churn/leak checks use qualitative language — "memory returns to roughly its starting point", "no unbounded growth" — with no concrete threshold. A slow leak (e.g. a few KB per surface-free that the free_text fix didn't fully address) could pass an eyeballed check release after release.
ELI10: "Roughly the same" isn't a number a future person can compare against — without a concrete threshold, gradual memory growth across several bumps could go unnoticed indefinitely.
Stakes if we pick wrong: leave it qualitative and a real slow leak ships silently; require exact numbers and you're asking for false-precision on a manual check that inherently has noise (backgrounded processes, Swift ARC timing).
Recommendation: 4B — record actual before/after RSS numbers (a real measurement) without demanding a rigid pass/fail threshold, since manual runs have too much variance for a hard number to be meaningful across machines.
Completeness: 4A=3/10, 4B=7/10, 4C=9/10.

options.label: 4C: Automate it with a hard threshold
options.description: Fold the leak check into the new XCUITest tripwire from finding 1 — loop surface create/destroy N times, assert RSS delta stays under a fixed bound (e.g. <5MB after 200 cycles). Most rigorous, but adds scope to the already-expanded finding 1B test and risks a flaky threshold across CI hardware.

options.label: 4A: Leave as qualitative
options.description: Keep "roughly its starting point" as-is — matches how the rest of QA-libghostty.md's manual checks are already worded. Effort: zero, but doesn't improve the fuzziness this finding identified.
