1	# Bump the libghostty pin (1.2.3 → 1.3.2)
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Workroom's terminal is `GhosttyKit.xcframework`, distributed by third-party wrapper
6	`Lakr233/libghostty-spm` and pinned exactly in `macapp/project.yml` (the embedding C API isn't
7	stable, so no floating version). We link only the raw `GhosttyKit` C-API product — our own
8	`GhosttySurfaceView.swift` (2001 lines) drives `ghostty_surface_*` directly; we don't consume the
9	wrapper's Swift convenience layer.
10	
11	Current pin: wrapper `1.2.3` (`df168f41`), built from upstream `ghostty-org/ghostty` engine
12	`332b2aef` (tag `v1.3.1`, 2026-03-13). Target: wrapper `1.3.2` (`b146b73a`), built from engine
13	`35e1a016` (untagged, 2026-07-10) — roughly four months and ~1300 commits of upstream fixes,
14	including two capabilities nothing else can reach: `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid`/`tty_name`
15	(blocked: CMT-1, "no PTY child PID") and `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` (an optimization path
16	for CMT-3's a11y hook, already shipped 2026-08-10 via a 400ms poll workaround).
17	
18	This bump is fully scoped already at `TODOS.md:104-232` ("Bump the libghostty pin") — that entry,
19	plus fresh research done this session (verified against actual source, not assumed), is the basis
20	for this plan. Two related decisions it surfaces (owning the xcframework build; adopting the
21	wrapper's `AppTerminalView` convenience layer) are filed as separate, deliberately-deferred TODOS.md
22	entries and are **not** part of this plan.
23	
24	**Hard gate — this plan does not execute past Phase 0 today.** `TODOS.md` scopes this as
25	"post-GA, first change after the GA tag." The repo is currently at `v2.0.0-beta.24`; no `v2.0.0`
26	tag exists. Phase 0 checks for that tag specifically (not any non-prerelease tag — `v1.0.0`
27	through `v1.3.0` already exist as unrelated pre-rewrite releases) and halts if absent.
28	
29	## Phase dependency diagram
30	
31	```
32	Phase 0 ── GA tag check ─────────────────────────────────────────┐
33	  (git tag == v2.0.0, exact — not any non-prerelease tag)        │
34	                                                                   │ halts here
35	                                                                   │ until GA ships
36	                                                                   ▼
37	Phase 1 ── Pre-bump baseline (current engine) ────────────────────┐
38	  QA-libghostty.md §N in full + SelectionGesture check            │
39	  + 2 new IO-layer items (scrollback-click race, free_text leak)  │
40	  RSS recorded (not "roughly") for every churn/leak item           │
41	                                                                   │ must run BEFORE
42	                                                                   │ Phase 2 — baseline
43	                                                                   │ after the bump is
44	                                                                   │ worthless (§N's
45	                                                                   │ own rule)
46	                                                                   ▼
47	Phase 2 ── Mechanical pin bump ────────────────────────────────────┐
48	  project.yml exactVersion → 1.3.2                                │
49	  Package.resolved regen (SPM resolve, never hand-edit)            │
50	  ⚠ assert resolved revision == b146b73a... exactly, or FAIL       │
51	  build once → modulemap-collision workaround still holds?         │
52	                                                                   ▼
53	Phase 3 ── Resource regeneration ──────────────────────────────────┐
54	  terminfo (expect no diff) │ shell-integration (expect upgrade)   │
55	  CHECKSUMS + SOURCE.md refresh │ GhosttyResourcesTests green       │
56	                                                                   ▼
57	Phase 4 ── SSH dispatch test ───────────────────────────────────────┐
58	  `+ssh --help` exit-0 test in GhosttyCLITests.swift                │
59	  (real-host SSH integration stays manual — separate decision,      │
60	   not blocking this bump)                                         │
61	                                                                   ▼
62	Phase 5 ── Post-bump retest (the actual regression gate) ──────────┐
63	  QA-libghostty.md §N re-run, diffed against Phase 1 baseline       │
64	  NEW: automated XCUITest tripwire (orphan-shell / EXC_BAD_ACCESS)  │
65	  GhosttyActionDispatchUITests re-run                               │
66	        │                                                           │
67	        ├─ if §N's "⌘F wrap + ordering" item shows drift ─┐         │
68	        │                                                  ▼         │
69	        │                              edit TerminalSearch.navigationPlan
70	        │                              (conditional — skip if unchanged)
71	        ▼                                                           ▼
72	Phase 6 ── Release gates ───────────────────────────────────────────┘
73	  local universal build sanity check (optional)
74	  land on master → nightly.yml bake gate (N clean nightlies, TBD)
75	
76	Commits: [Doc hygiene] lands independently, before or alongside Phase 1-2.
77	         [The bump] = Phases 2-4 in one commit (TODOS.md: "same commit").
78	         Phase 1 (baseline) and Phase 5 (retest) are QA passes, not commits.
79	```
80	
81	## What's corrected vs. what TODOS.md currently says
82	
83	- `QA-libghostty.md` already has a full "§N Engine bump smoke" section (`QA-libghostty.md:137-216`,
84	  4 subsections) — TODOS.md's "Also required" bullet claiming it "needs to be created" is stale.
85	  Its own preamble also states the baseline must be run **before** the bump, not after — the current
86	  plan phasing (below) respects that.
87	- `WorkroomApp.swift:606` (cited by both TODOS.md and QA-libghostty.md for the EXC_BAD_ACCESS
88	  teardown comment) has drifted — the actual comment is now at `WorkroomApp.swift:665-678`.
89	- Two upstream fixes not yet in either doc: `ghostty_surface_free_text` was silently not freeing
90	  memory (now fixed — our 4 call sites in `GhosttySurfaceView.swift` need no code change, just a
91	  leak sanity-check); a `mouseButtonCallback`/scrollback-pruning race (use-after-free on link
92	  clicks) is fixed — worth a targeted regression check.
93	- Two real C-ABI removals upstream (`ghostty_app_key_is_binding`, `ghostty_input_trigger_u.translated`)
94	  — grepped the whole app, zero call sites for either. Zero risk, no action needed.
95	- The CI xcbuild cache (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has no `restore-keys` fallback — only the SPM
96	  cache does. A revert only needs to worry about the SPM cache carrying stale state.
97	
98	## Phase 1 — Pre-bump baseline (before touching anything)
99	
100	Run `QA-libghostty.md` §N in full against the **current** engine and record results — its own
101	preamble requires this, since several items only have a "same as before" pass criterion. Also run
102	the `SelectionGesture` drag/click-threshold check (TODOS.md:170) even though it's not in §N today,
103	since the upstream rewrite touches exactly that path.
104	
105	**Reword the existing "IO layer" checklist items** (`QA-libghostty.md:150-163`) to record actual
106	measurements instead of eyeballing: "Surface churn" and "Orphan check" currently say "memory
107	returns to roughly its starting point" / implicitly rely on a qualitative read — change both to
108	"record RSS before and after (Activity Monitor or `vmmap`), note the delta" so a slow leak across
109	several future bumps is comparable, not just eyeballed. No hard pass/fail threshold — manual-run
110	variance (background processes, ARC timing) would make a rigid number meaningless across machines.
111	
112	Add two new checklist items to §N's "IO layer" subsection now, with the same RSS-recording wording,
113	and baseline them too:
114	- Select/click text while scrollback is actively producing output (regression target for the
115	  `mouseButtonCallback` race fix).
116	- A `ghostty_surface_free_text` leak spot-check: loop `readFullSurface`/`readSelectionText`
117	  (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:792-857`) a few hundred times, record RSS before/after.
118	
119	## Phase 2 — Mechanical pin bump
120	
121	- `macapp/project.yml:48-68`: change `exactVersion: 1.2.3` → `1.3.2`, and rewrite the comment block
122	  (it's the documented single source of truth) to state package `1.3.2` / engine `35e1a016`.
123	- Regenerate `Package.resolved` (`macapp/WorkroomApp.xcodeproj/project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved`)
124	  via Xcode/`xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies` after `make app-generate` — never hand-edit;
125	  it carries an `originHash` SwiftPM manages.
126	- **Assert the resolved revision, don't trust the tag.** Immediately after resolution, grep the
127	  regenerated `Package.resolved` for `libghostty-spm`'s `revision` field and hard-fail if it isn't
128	  exactly `b146b73a8ba3ed2678a22a9de5feecfcbf298d48`. This packager has re-cut an already-published
129	  tag before (arm64e slices shipped 2026-07-21, reverted 3 days later under the same tag) — a moved
130	  `1.3.2` tag would silently vendor a different engine than everything in this plan was researched
131	  against.
132	- Clear `macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages` for a clean resolve (stale-cache risk cuts both ways).
133	- Build once and confirm the modulemap-collision workaround (`macapp/CLAUDE.md:120-124`, "Multiple
134	  commands produce include/module.modulemap") still holds under the new xcframework's header layout
135	  — a build failure here surfaces immediately, no separate step needed to detect it.
136	- Confirm the build compiles clean against the new header. Do **not** wire
137	  `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid`/`tty_name` or a `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` case in
138	  `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.handleAction` (`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift:25-141`) — both are separate,
139	  already-tracked follow-ups (CMT-1, CMT-3-optimization), not part of this bump. The new action tag
140	  falling into the existing `default:` arm (logs once in Debug) is expected and fine.
141	
142	## Phase 3 — Resource regeneration
143	
144	- Clone `ghostty-org/ghostty` at `35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58`.
145	- `terminfo/`: per `Resources/ghostty/SOURCE.md:30-43` this is currently byte-identical to the
146	  engine's own — diff against the new checkout to confirm still true; do not blindly regenerate.
147	- `shell-integration/`: copy with `cp -RL` (dereference — `GhosttyResourcesTests` hard-fails on any
148	  symlink in a tracked subtree). Current scripts are pinned ~12-52 days ahead of the *old* engine on
149	  purpose (SOURCE.md:45-71); since the new engine commit is from 2026-07-10, regenerating is expected
150	  to be a strict upgrade — diff to confirm none of the 4 documented upstream fixes regress.
151	- Keep `terminfo/67/ghostty` a byte-identical **copy** of `terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty` (not upstream's
152	  symlink) — required by `GhosttyResourcesTests.testTerminfoAliasMatchesPrimaryEntry`.
153	- Regenerate `Resources/ghostty/CHECKSUMS` (`shasum -a 256`, terminfo + shell-integration only —
154	  never `themes/`, which has its own separate `CHECKSUMS`/`SOURCE.md` and must not be touched).
155	- Update `SOURCE.md`: refresh the Provenance "measured against" pin, the shell-integration
156	  blob-hash/commit-range table, and resolve the ssh-wrapper section now that `+ssh` genuinely exists
157	  at this pin (it doesn't at v1.3.1).
158	- Run `GhosttyResourcesTests` locally — all four assertions (checksum match both directions, no
159	  unexpected top-level entries, themes excluded, alias byte-identical) must pass.
160	
161	## Phase 4 — SSH dispatch test
162	
163	- Add a dispatch test to `GhosttyCLITests.swift` (mirrors `testGhosttyRunsSshCacheActionAndWritesCache`
164	  at line 91): run `["+ssh", "--help"]` via the existing `runGhostty` helper, assert exit 0 — this
165	  matches TODOS.md's explicit spec ("asserted the way `release.sh` already asserts `+ssh-cache`",
166	  confirmed at `release.sh:212-216` to be exit-code-based) — and additionally assert stdout contains
167	  expected help text where cheap, consistent with how `testGhosttyRejectsInvalidAction` goes beyond
168	  a bare exit code.
169	- **Explicitly deferred (Step 0 scope decision):** a real end-to-end test that actually SSHes through
170	  the regenerated wrapper to a real host — no sshd/docker/expect test infrastructure exists anywhere
171	  in this repo today, and building it is genuinely separable from the bump itself. Stays the manual
172	  QA step it already is (`QA-libghostty.md:187-199`, "ssh integration" — already scoped as "the part
173	  that needs a real remote host"). File as its own follow-up task if worth automating later; not
174	  blocking this bump.
175	
176	## Phase 5 — Post-bump retest (the actual regression gate)
177	
178	No automated test today covers high-volume surface churn, the literal `ps` orphan-shell check, or
179	anything asserting the EXC_BAD_ACCESS teardown race (`WorkroomApp.swift:665-678`) — confirmed by
180	direct search. Per eng-review finding 1, this bump adds one automated tripwire rather than leaving
181	it fully manual:
182	
183	- **New XCUITest: orphan-shell / teardown regression.** Add a test (new method in an existing
184	  lifecycle-relevant UI test file, or a new file if none fits cleanly — survey
185	  `WorkroomWorkflowUITests.swift` and `SplitPaneUITests.swift` first for the right home) that:
186	  drives the running app to open a pane, spawn a real shell running a TUI (`vim` or similar, same
187	  scenario as `QA-libghostty.md:162`), quits the app via the UI, then — from the test process itself,
188	  same `Process()`-driving pattern already established in `GhosttyCLITests.swift:36-62` — shells out
189	  to `ps -ax` and asserts no `zsh`/`bash` survives. This is new process-assertion territory for
190	  `WorkroomAppUITests` (no existing test asserts on OS-level process state), so budget real design
191	  time, not a copy-paste. Does not replace the manual §N checklist (churn volume, force-quit variant,
192	  workroom-switch scenarios stay manual) — it's the one automated tripwire for the single worst
193	  failure mode (a broken IO patch silently orphaning shells).
194	- Re-run `QA-libghostty.md` §N in full against the new engine and diff against the Phase 1 baseline —
195	  including the two new IO-layer items and the `SelectionGesture` check added in Phase 1.
196	- Name the automated half of the gate explicitly rather than leaving it implicit: TODOS.md's
197	  "XCUITest action-tag baseline" is `GhosttyActionDispatchUITests.testRunningCommandRetitlesTheTabChip`
198	  and `testOSCProgressReportMarksTheTabBusyThenIdle` (lines 97, 118) — run these against the new
199	  engine as the automated pass/fail complement to §N.
200	- `TerminalSearch.navigationPlan` (`TerminalSearch.swift:70-83`): touch this **only if** §N's
201	  "⌘F wrap + ordering" item reveals actual behavior change (direction, wrap point, or match-order
202	  semantics). If unchanged, no code or test edit needed — record that it was checked.
203	
204	## Phase 6 — Release gates (mostly already-existing machinery, not new work)
205	
206	- Local sanity check before pushing (optional signal): `VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal make app-vcs`,
207	  then `xcodebuild -configuration Release ARCHS="arm64 x86_64" ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=NO build`.
208	- Land on `master`. `nightly.yml` already runs `make app-test` (gate) → `make app-release`
209	  (universal, notarized) daily — this is the bake gate. Decide how many clean nightlies to require
210	  before promoting to a `pre` tag (not specified anywhere today — your call at that point).
211	- Do not remove the backspace-DEL-as-text (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:1171`) or ⌃Tab workarounds
212	  until baked — both fail safe either way, so removal needs its own raw-PTY probe, not this bump.
213	
214	## Rollback
215	
216	Revert the commit(s), `rm -rf macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages`, rebuild. Only the CI **SPM** cache
217	(`ci.yml`, `restore-keys: spm-${os}-`) risks restoring stale state on a revert — the xcbuild cache
218	has no restore-keys fallback, so a revert is just a clean cache miss there, nothing to bust.
219	
220	## Commits
221	
222	1. **Doc hygiene first, standalone** (land before the bump so whoever reads TODOS.md next sees
223	   correct state): fix the two stale line references (`WorkroomApp.swift:606` → `665-678`) in both
224	   `TODOS.md` and `QA-libghostty.md`, and correct TODOS.md's "§N needs to be created" claim.
225	2. **The bump itself, one commit** (Phases 2-4 — TODOS.md itself frames pin + resources + ssh tests
226	   as "same commit"): `project.yml`, `Package.resolved`, `Resources/ghostty/*`, `GhosttyCLITests.swift`.
227	   The real-host SSH integration test stays a separate, later decision — not part of this commit.
228	3. **The new orphan-shell XCUITest, its own commit** (Phase 5's finding-1 tripwire) — new test
229	   infrastructure deserves review separately from the mechanical pin/resource bump, even though both
230	   land before the same bake period.
231	4. Phase 1 (baseline) and Phase 5 (retest) are manual QA passes, not commits — their only artifact
232	   is the recorded §N results and the checklist additions from Phase 1 (which land as part of commit 1
233	   or 2, whichever is more convenient at execution time).
234	
235	## Verification
236	
237	- `make app-test` green, including `GhosttyResourcesTests` (all 4 assertions) and the new
238	  `GhosttyCLITests` `+ssh --help` dispatch test.
239	- Phase 2's revision-match assertion actually fires against a deliberately-wrong expected sha once,
240	  to prove it's a real check and not a no-op before relying on it.
241	- The new orphan-shell XCUITest (Phase 5) passes against the new engine, and — as a sanity check that
242	  it can actually fail — passes against the *old* pinned engine too before the bump lands (proves the
243	  test isn't vacuously green because the app already worked, or because the test never really exercises
244	  teardown).
245	- `QA-libghostty.md` §N fully re-run against the new engine, diffed against the Phase 1 baseline —
246	  the manual complement to the new automated tripwire above.
247	- `GhosttyActionDispatchUITests`'s two named tests pass against the new engine.
248	- Universal Release build links (`lipo -info` shows both slices) — either via the local sanity
249	  check or by trusting `nightly.yml`'s daily run.

result.output:
- Phase 0 does not enforce “first change after GA.” A local `v2.0.0` tag may be stale, unrelated to `HEAD`, or followed by other commits. Require the tag to be reachable from the target branch, pushed, and the bump branch based directly on the tagged commit.

- The target will be stale by execution time. The plan is intentionally blocked until an unknown future GA date, yet freezes today’s wrapper version, commit, ABI research, and resource expectations. Re-evaluate the latest wrapper and upstream delta after GA instead of mechanically executing this plan.

- The bump’s stated benefits are explicitly deferred. It takes on ~1,300 commits from an untagged engine snapshot while shipping neither foreground-PID support nor selection-change handling. That is poor post-GA risk/reward unless the engine fixes independently justify an immediate bump.

- The ABI review is inadequate. Grepping for two removed symbols only proves those two removals are harmless. It does not cover changed struct layouts, enum values, callback contracts, ownership, thread affinity, deployment targets, or architecture slices. Diff the complete exported headers and binary metadata before runtime QA.

- The orphan-process XCUITest is fundamentally invalid as specified. `ps -ax` plus “no zsh/bash” will detect unrelated shells, miss `fish`, `vim`, and other descendants, and fail under parallel CI. Launch a uniquely marked process, prove its exact PID/process group is alive before quitting, then poll for that same process group to disappear.

- “The test passes against the old engine” does not prove it can fail. It proves only compatibility. Non-vacuity requires fault injection, temporarily disabling teardown, or another controlled condition that leaves the marked child alive.

- The test conflates UI quit, XCTest termination, graceful shutdown, and crash/force-quit behavior. Those exercise different teardown paths. Specify which path is under test; the worst reported failure mode is not covered merely by one normal UI quit.

questions.question:
CROSS-MODEL TENSION 6 — Codex disagrees with eng-review finding 4's decision (record RSS numbers, no hard threshold). Codex: "a few hundred free_text calls may be below measurement noise, while allocator retention can look like a leak" — without instrumentation or a defined bound, the check can't actually distinguish a real leak from normal allocator behavior. Similarly the scrollback-click race check ("click once during output") won't reliably reproduce a timing-dependent use-after-free — that needs repeatable stress, ideally under a memory diagnostic tool.
ELI10: Finding 4 already softened these checks to "just write down the number" because manual runs are noisy — Codex is saying that's not soft, it's toothless: a real leak and normal noise would look identical without real tooling.
Stakes if we pick wrong: keep it soft and a real leak/race ships invisibly; add real tooling and you're now asking for Instruments/leak-detector expertise on what was meant to be a lightweight manual QA pass.
Recommendation: 6B — upgrade specifically the free_text leak check to use Xcode's Instruments (Leaks template) or a scripted `leaks` CLI run instead of eyeballed RSS — that tool exists precisely for this and isn't much more setup than Activity Monitor. Leave the scrollback-click race as manual repeated-clicking (repeatable stress under Instruments is disproportionate for a one-off regression spot-check); accept it as directionally useful, not rigorous.
Completeness: A=4/10, B=8/10, C=9/10 (full rigor on both, more setup cost).

# Bump the libghostty pin (1.2.3 → 1.3.2)

## Context

Workroom's terminal is `GhosttyKit.xcframework`, distributed by third-party wrapper
`Lakr233/libghostty-spm` and pinned exactly in `macapp/project.yml` (the embedding C API isn't
stable, so no floating version). We link only the raw `GhosttyKit` C-API product — our own
`GhosttySurfaceView.swift` (2001 lines) drives `ghostty_surface_*` directly; we don't consume the
wrapper's Swift convenience layer.

Current pin: wrapper `1.2.3` (`df168f41`), built from upstream `ghostty-org/ghostty` engine
`332b2aef` (tag `v1.3.1`, 2026-03-13). Target: wrapper `1.3.2` (`b146b73a`), built from engine
`35e1a016` (untagged, 2026-07-10) — roughly four months and ~1300 commits of upstream fixes,
including two capabilities nothing else can reach: `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid`/`tty_name`
(blocked: CMT-1, "no PTY child PID") and `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` (an optimization path
for CMT-3's a11y hook, already shipped 2026-08-10 via a 400ms poll workaround).

This bump is fully scoped already at `TODOS.md:104-232` ("Bump the libghostty pin") — that entry,
plus fresh research done this session (verified against actual source, not assumed), is the basis
for this plan. Two related decisions it surfaces (owning the xcframework build; adopting the
wrapper's `AppTerminalView` convenience layer) are filed as separate, deliberately-deferred TODOS.md
entries and are **not** part of this plan.

**GA gate removed (2026-08-12 decision, reversing an earlier call this session).** `TODOS.md`
originally scoped this as "post-GA, first change after the GA tag" — the repo is still at
`v2.0.0-beta.24`, no `v2.0.0` tag exists. You've explicitly decided to proceed ahead of GA. This
plan is executable now; there is no Phase 0 halt. `TODOS.md`'s entry needs its "post-GA" framing
and "Depends on: GA shipping first" line updated to match — do that alongside landing this bump,
so the tracking doc doesn't contradict what actually shipped.

## Phase dependency diagram

```
Phase 1 ── Pre-bump baseline (current engine) ────────────────────┐
  QA-libghostty.md §N in full + SelectionGesture check            │
  + 2 new IO-layer items (scrollback-click race, free_text leak)  │
  RSS recorded (not "roughly") for every churn/leak item           │
                                                                   │ must run BEFORE
                                                                   │ Phase 2 — baseline
                                                                   │ after the bump is
                                                                   │ worthless (§N's
                                                                   │ own rule)
                                                                   ▼
Phase 2 ── Mechanical pin bump ────────────────────────────────────┐
  project.yml exactVersion → 1.3.2                                │
  Package.resolved regen (SPM resolve, never hand-edit)            │
  ⚠ assert resolved revision == b146b73a... exactly, or FAIL       │
  build once → modulemap-collision workaround still holds?         │
                                                                   ▼
Phase 3 ── Resource regeneration ──────────────────────────────────┐
  terminfo (expect no diff) │ shell-integration (expect upgrade)   │
  CHECKSUMS + SOURCE.md refresh │ GhosttyResourcesTests green       │
                                                                   ▼
Phase 4 ── SSH dispatch test ───────────────────────────────────────┐
  `+ssh --help` exit-0 test in GhosttyCLITests.swift                │
  (real-host SSH integration stays manual — separate decision,      │
   not blocking this bump)                                         │
                                                                   ▼
Phase 5 ── Post-bump retest (the actual regression gate) ──────────┐
  QA-libghostty.md §N re-run, diffed against Phase 1 baseline       │
  NEW: automated XCUITest tripwire (orphan-shell / EXC_BAD_ACCESS)  │
  GhosttyActionDispatchUITests re-run                               │
        │                                                           │
        ├─ if §N's "⌘F wrap + ordering" item shows drift ─┐         │
        │                                                  ▼         │
        │                              edit TerminalSearch.navigationPlan
        │                              (conditional — skip if unchanged)
        ▼                                                           ▼
Phase 6 ── Release gates ───────────────────────────────────────────┘
  local universal build sanity check (optional)
  land on master → nightly.yml bake gate (N clean nightlies, TBD)

Commits: [Doc hygiene] lands independently, before or alongside Phase 1-2.
         [The bump] = Phases 2-4 in one commit (TODOS.md: "same commit").
         Phase 1 (baseline) and Phase 5 (retest) are QA passes, not commits.
```

## What's corrected vs. what TODOS.md currently says

- `QA-libghostty.md` already has a full "§N Engine bump smoke" section (`QA-libghostty.md:137-216`,
  4 subsections) — TODOS.md's "Also required" bullet claiming it "needs to be created" is stale.
  Its own preamble also states the baseline must be run **before** the bump, not after — the current
  plan phasing (below) respects that.
- `WorkroomApp.swift:606` (cited by both TODOS.md and QA-libghostty.md for the EXC_BAD_ACCESS
  teardown comment) has drifted — the actual comment is now at `WorkroomApp.swift:665-678`.
- Two upstream fixes not yet in either doc: `ghostty_surface_free_text` was silently not freeing
  memory (now fixed — our 4 call sites in `GhosttySurfaceView.swift` need no code change, just a
  leak sanity-check); a `mouseButtonCallback`/scrollback-pruning race (use-after-free on link
  clicks) is fixed — worth a targeted regression check.
- Two real C-ABI removals upstream (`ghostty_app_key_is_binding`, `ghostty_input_trigger_u.translated`)
  — grepped the whole app, zero call sites for either. Zero risk, no action needed.
- The CI xcbuild cache (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has no `restore-keys` fallback — only the SPM
  cache does. A revert only needs to worry about the SPM cache carrying stale state.

## Phase 1 — Pre-bump baseline (before touching anything)

Run `QA-libghostty.md` §N in full against the **current** engine and record results — its own
preamble requires this, since several items only have a "same as before" pass criterion. Also run
the `SelectionGesture` drag/click-threshold check (TODOS.md:170) even though it's not in §N today,
since the upstream rewrite touches exactly that path.

**Give the baseline a durable home** (Codex cross-model tension 9 — "recorded" with no defined
location means the next bump has nothing concrete to diff against). Write results to a checked-in,
dated file — `macapp/QA-libghostty-results/<date>-libghostty-1.3.2-bump.md` — capturing: commit
hash, OS version, architecture, machine, and the actual measurement method/numbers for every §N item
and the new Instruments/leaks output. Phase 5 writes its results to the same file (baseline vs.
post-bump, side by side) so a future bump has an actual precedent to compare against, not just this
plan's prose.

**Reword the existing "IO layer" checklist items** (`QA-libghostty.md:150-163`) to record actual
measurements instead of eyeballing: "Surface churn" and "Orphan check" currently say "memory
returns to roughly its starting point" / implicitly rely on a qualitative read — change both to
"record RSS before and after (Activity Monitor or `vmmap`), note the delta" so a slow leak across
several future bumps is comparable, not just eyeballed. No hard pass/fail threshold — manual-run
variance (background processes, ARC timing) would make a rigid number meaningless across machines.

Add two new checklist items to §N's "IO layer" subsection now, and baseline them too:
- Select/click text while scrollback is actively producing output (regression target for the
  `mouseButtonCallback` race fix), same RSS-recording wording as the reworded items above.
- A `ghostty_surface_free_text` leak spot-check: loop `readFullSurface`/`readSelectionText`
  (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:792-857`) a few hundred times — **upgraded per Codex cross-model
  tension**: RSS alone can't distinguish a real leak from normal allocator retention at this scale.
  Use Xcode's Instruments (Leaks template) or a scripted `leaks <pid>` CLI run around the loop
  instead of eyeballing RSS — proportionate tooling that exists precisely for this, not much more
  setup than Activity Monitor.

## Phase 2 — Mechanical pin bump

- **Full ABI diff before touching anything else** (eng-review finding 4, Codex cross-model tension).
  This session's ABI check only grepped for two known removed symbols
  (`ghostty_app_key_is_binding`, `ghostty_input_trigger_u.translated`) against our own call sites —
  it did not diff the complete `include/ghostty.h` for struct-layout changes, enum value changes,
  callback-contract changes, ownership/thread-affinity changes, or deployment-target/arch-slice
  changes between `332b2aef` and `35e1a016`. Diff the full header (both revisions already fetched
  this session) before relying on Phase 5's runtime QA to catch anything — a struct-layout mismatch
  is exactly the class of bug that compiles clean and passes casual testing, then corrupts memory
  later. If the diff surfaces anything beyond the two already-verified-safe removals, stop and
  investigate before proceeding to the rest of this phase.
- `macapp/project.yml:48-68`: change `exactVersion: 1.2.3` → `1.3.2`, and rewrite the comment block
  (it's the documented single source of truth) to state package `1.3.2` / engine `35e1a016`.
- Regenerate `Package.resolved` (`macapp/WorkroomApp.xcodeproj/project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved`)
  via Xcode/`xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies` after `make app-generate` — never hand-edit;
  it carries an `originHash` SwiftPM manages.
- **Assert the resolved revision as a permanent test, not a one-time grep** (Codex cross-model
  tension 8 — a manual check protects only this bump; a checked-in test protects every future one).
  Add a small XCTest (e.g. in `GhosttyResourcesTests.swift` or a new lightweight test) that reads
  `Package.resolved` and asserts `libghostty-spm`'s `revision` equals the constant
  `b146b73a8ba3ed2678a22a9de5feecfcbf298d48`, so it runs on every `make app-test` going forward. This
  packager has re-cut an already-published tag before (arm64e slices shipped 2026-07-21, reverted 3
  days later under the same tag) — a moved tag would silently vendor a different engine than what's
  actually reviewed. The test is *expected* to need updating on the next pin bump — that's the point,
  it forces whoever does that bump to notice and deliberately update the constant, not silently drift.
- Clear `macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages` for a clean resolve (stale-cache risk cuts both ways).
- Build once and confirm the modulemap-collision workaround (`macapp/CLAUDE.md:120-124`, "Multiple
  commands produce include/module.modulemap") still holds under the new xcframework's header layout
  — a build failure here surfaces immediately, no separate step needed to detect it.
- Confirm the build compiles clean against the new header. Do **not** wire
  `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid`/`tty_name` or a `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` case in
  `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.handleAction` (`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift:25-141`) — both are separate,
  already-tracked follow-ups (CMT-1, CMT-3-optimization), not part of this bump. The new action tag
  falling into the existing `default:` arm (logs once in Debug) is expected and fine.

## Phase 3 — Resource regeneration

- Clone `ghostty-org/ghostty` at `35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58`.
- `terminfo/`: per `Resources/ghostty/SOURCE.md:30-43` this is currently byte-identical to the
  engine's own — diff against the new checkout to confirm still true; do not blindly regenerate.
- `shell-integration/`: copy with `cp -RL` (dereference — `GhosttyResourcesTests` hard-fails on any
  symlink in a tracked subtree). Current scripts are pinned ~12-52 days ahead of the *old* engine on

## Worktree parallelization strategy

Sequential implementation, no parallelization opportunity. Every phase after Phase 2 depends on the
pin actually being bumped (Phase 3's resource regen needs the new ref decided; Phase 4/5's tests need
the new build to run against), and Phase 1's baseline must complete before Phase 2 starts (§N's own
rule). The one piece that's genuinely independent — the new orphan-shell XCUITest's design work
(tension 5) — could theoretically be prototyped against the *current* engine in parallel with Phase
1-2, but its non-vacuity proof (running against deliberately-disabled teardown) and its "does it pass
against the new engine" check both need the bump to have happened first, so the time saved is marginal
against the coordination cost. Not worth splitting across worktrees.

       ///

       /// the hangup and is left orphaned on its port/pidfile. So `applicationShouldTerminate` Ctrl-Cs
       /// every live run command and waits for it to exit *before* returning — sending key events only,
       /// never freeing a surface, so the no-mass-free rationale above still holds (issue #7, Option B).
       @MainActor
       func applicationWillTerminate(_ notification: Notification) {}

# --- macOS app (macapp/) ---

# The Debug product is "Workroom Dev" (distinct bundle id + name) so it runs alongside the
# installed release "Workroom" without conflict — see macapp/project.yml.
APP_PROJECT := WorkroomApp.xcodeproj
APP_NAME    := Workroom Dev
APP_BUNDLE  := DerivedData/Build/Products/Debug/$(APP_NAME).app
APP_XCODEBUILD := xcodebuild -project $(APP_PROJECT) -scheme WorkroomApp -configuration Debug \
  -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages

# Extra xcodebuild build-setting overrides, appended to app-build/app-test. Empty locally so
# ⌘R-style automatic signing is used; CI sets this to ad-hoc / no-team signing because hosted
# runners have no signing cert or DEVELOPMENT_TEAM (e.g.
# `make app-test APP_SIGN_FLAGS="CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="`).
APP_SIGN_FLAGS ?=

# Extra xcodebuild options for app-test. Parallel execution by default: the suite is dominated by a
# few slow integration classes (Markdown WebView renders, real git/jj repos), so spreading classes
# across worker processes cuts the run ~40% (48s -> ~29s). Each worker gets its own host-app process
# but they share one UserDefaults domain, so a test mutating a `Defaults` key another class reads
# would race — override with `make app-test APP_TEST_FLAGS=` to bisect a suspected parallel-only
# failure. Test dirs are already UUID-scoped under NSTemporaryDirectory, so those don't collide.
APP_TEST_FLAGS ?= -parallel-testing-enabled YES

# Extra xcodebuild options for app-uitest. Skips the 3 most expensive/flaky cases by default (each
# does a real quit+relaunch or a hard timing budget), since XCUITest never runs in CI and a routine
# `make app-uitest` was paying ~4-5 min for tests that are only load-bearing right before a release.
# The isolation-tripwire tests those two classes carried (proving discovery/session-restore no-op
# without a seeded path — a guard the REST of this suite depends on) were extracted to
# `AgentSessionIsolationTripwireUITests` first, so the routine sweep keeps that safety net. Run the
# full suite (pre-release, or after touching any of these) with `make app-uitest APP_UITEST_FLAGS=`.
APP_UITEST_FLAGS ?= -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/SessionRestoreUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/HistoryStressUITests/testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/WindowDragUITests/testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips

# The Rust VCS core (jj-lib via UniFFI) the app links, built into the local WrVcs SwiftPM package
# (vcs/swift/WrVcs). Must run before xcodegen so the package's xcframework + generated Swift exist.
# arm64 by default; release/distribution sets VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal (needs rustup stable >=
# 1.93 + both darwin targets, and `protoc` on PATH for jj-lib's build).
VCS_APPLE_FLAGS ?=
app-vcs: ## Build the Rust VCS core (xcframework + Swift bindings) the app links
	vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh $(VCS_APPLE_FLAGS)

app-run: app-build ## Build (Debug) and launch the dev app, replacing any running dev instance
	cd macapp || exit 1; \
	pkill -x "$(APP_NAME)" 2>/dev/null || true; \
	i=0; \
	while pgrep -x "$(APP_NAME)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ $$i -lt 40 ]; do \
	  sleep 0.2; i=$$((i + 1)); \
	done; \
	echo "Launching $(APP_BUNDLE)"; \
	open "$(APP_BUNDLE)"

app-build: app-vcs ## Build the app (Debug)
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && $(APP_XCODEBUILD) build $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-test: app-vcs ## Run the app's unit tests
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && $(APP_XCODEBUILD) -destination 'platform=macOS' $(APP_TEST_FLAGS) test $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-uitest: app-vcs ## Run the app's UI tests (XCUITest — needs a real GUI login session, not headless)
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project $(APP_PROJECT) -scheme WorkroomAppUITests -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages -destination 'platform=macOS' $(APP_UITEST_FLAGS) test $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-test-supervisor: ## Run the run-command supervisor PTY integration test (real shell + fake server)
	python3 macapp/Tests/run-supervisor/test_supervisor.py

app-test-scripts: ## Run the dependency-free shell-script tests (build-helper archs, channel classify)
	sh macapp/Scripts/build-helper_test.sh
	sh macapp/Scripts/channel-helper_test.sh

app-generate: app-vcs ## Force-regenerate the (gitignored) .xcodeproj from project.yml
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate

app-format: ## Format Swift sources in place (swift-format)
	cd macapp && xcrun swift-format format --in-place --parallel --recursive WorkroomApp WorkroomAppTests WorkroomAppUITests

app-lint: ## Lint Swift with swift-format (--strict)
	cd macapp && xcrun swift-format lint --strict --parallel --recursive WorkroomApp WorkroomAppTests WorkroomAppUITests

485	  /// Force a deterministic **UI** state in fixture mode: the inspector open, parked on
486	  /// `inspectorSection` with every section expanded, and the diff viewer in `diffViewMode`. Must be
487	  /// called before any `AppStore` is built (`WorkroomApp.init`), because `activeInspectorSection` and
488	  /// the layout both seed themselves from `Defaults` at construction.
489	  ///
490	  /// These are all `Defaults` keys in the app's real (Dev) UserDefaults domain, so without this a
491	  /// test inherits whatever the developer last left behind. That is not hypothetical: a collapsed
492	  /// section renders only its header, a closed inspector has nothing at all, and a `Dev`
493	  /// domain holding `diffViewMode = sideBySide` turned three `DiffViewerUITests` + two
494	  /// `DiffHighlightUITests` red for weeks — they assert on `diff.line`, which only the *unified*
495	  /// renderer emits, and read "the global default" from a pref the developer can change in Settings.
496	  ///
497	  /// The cost of pinning is that a fixture launch **overwrites** these keys in the Dev domain (it
498	  /// can't be a plain read: the views take them from `Defaults`). Dev is its own domain, so this
499	  /// never touches the release app's preferences — but a UI-test run does reset the Dev app's
500	  /// inspector and diff-mode choices, which is the deliberate trade for hermetic tests.
501	  ///
502	  /// A launch argument can't do this job. Argument-domain values arrive as **strings**
503	  /// (`-showNotificationsInspector 1` stores `"1"`, not `true`), and `Defaults` reads a natively
504	  /// supported type with `as? Bool`, which fails on a string and hands back the key's default
505	  /// (`false`) — so the argument doesn't just fail to force the pane open, it *pins it shut*: the
506	  /// argument domain outranks the app domain, so it also shadows the persisted value AND every
507	  /// later write (`AppStore.apply(.iconClick)`), leaving the pane unopenable for the whole run.
508	  /// `UITestFixture`'s own flags survive that only because `UserDefaults.bool(forKey:)` coerces
509	  /// strings. Hence a fixture-namespaced argument mirrored into `Defaults` here instead.
510	  ///
511	  /// `active` is a parameter, defaulting to the real flag, purely so its unit tests never have to
512	  /// WRITE `WorkroomUITestFixture`. Around 47 production sites branch on that key, including
513	  /// `AppStore.handleRootBranchChange`'s `guard !UITestFixture.isActive`, and `-parallel-testing`
514	  /// workers are separate processes sharing one on-disk defaults domain — so a class holding the key
515	  /// true for the length of a test body silently early-returns another class's history refresh, in a
516	  /// worker whose diff has nothing to do with any of this. That is the same cross-worker hazard
517	  /// `AppStore.confirmOnCloseOverrideForTesting` exists for; passing the state in avoids it at the
518	  /// source instead of racing and cleaning up.
519	  static func applyFixtureDefaults(active: Bool = isActive) {
520	    guard active else { return }
521	    Defaults[.showInspector] = true
522	    Defaults[.activeInspectorSection] = inspectorSection
523	    Defaults[.diffViewMode] = diffViewMode
524	    // Pinned to their `DefaultsKeys` defaults, for the same reason as the booleans above: a dragged
525	    // resize PERSISTS (real Dev domain, not fixture-isolated), and a fixture launch otherwise inherits
526	    // whatever an earlier drag-resize test left. Found chasing `DiffViewerUITests.
527	    // testSideBySideRendersTwoColumns`: the real domain had drifted to inspector.width=406/
528	    // sidebar.width=281 (vs. the 300/270 defaults), narrowing the detail column below
529	    // `DiffViewer.sideBySideMinWidth` (700) even at the fixture's otherwise-deterministic window width.
530	    Defaults[.sidebarWidth] = 270
531	    Defaults[.inspectorWidth] = 300
532	    // Every section expanded, equal heights. Not optional book-keeping: collapse state decides whether
533	    // a section's BODY renders at all (a collapsed section keeps only its header), and it's global +
534	    // persisted, so without this a test inherits whichever sections the developer — or the last UI test
535	    // to press ⌥⌘C/⌥⌘Y — left shut, and reads as "the panel is broken".
536	    Defaults[.inspectorLayout] = .default
537	    // Workroom's own last-fetch stamps, for the same reason as the collapse state: they PERSIST, and a
538	    // fetch performed by an earlier test writes one. `RemoteStateModel` takes the later of the backend's
539	    // evidence and this stamp, so a leftover value silently overrode a seeded `.never` and the
540	    // never-fetched state reported "just now" instead.
541	    Defaults[.vcsLastFetch] = [:]
542	    // The theme family, for the same reason as the collapse state and the fetch stamps: it PERSISTS.
543	    // Without this a theme test inherits whatever the developer last picked, and a test that applies
544	    // a theme leaves it applied for the next run.
545	    Defaults[.themeFamily] = themeFamily
546	  }

548	  /// The fake project list. Idempotent within a launch: the backing temp directories are created if
549	  /// missing so each target's terminal can start a shell. The project is reported as `git` — or as `jj`
550	  /// under `jjProject`, which is what the jj-wording tests need — so the sidebar's root row renders
551	  /// normally; no real VCS call is ever made either way (loading is short-circuited in `AppStore`, which
552	  /// also skips branch resolution for these paths).
553	  static func projects() -> [Project] {
554	    // Empty list for the no-projects scenario (issue #81 D3) — nothing to create or select.
555	    if noProjects { return [] }
556	    // One value for the project AND every workroom in it — a project with a mixed backend isn't a thing,
557	    // and a workroom disagreeing with its project would exercise a state the product can't reach.
558	    let vcs = jjProject ? "jj" : "git"
559	    let base = URL(fileURLWithPath: NSTemporaryDirectory(), isDirectory: true)
560	      .appendingPathComponent("workroom-uitest", isDirectory: true)
561	    let projectDir = base.appendingPathComponent(projectName, isDirectory: true)
562	    let workroomsBase = base.appendingPathComponent("workrooms", isDirectory: true)
563	    let workroomDir = workroomsBase.appendingPathComponent(workroomName, isDirectory: true)
564	    // A second workroom only for the drag/reorder scenario, so the tab bar has two chips to swap.
565	    let workroomDir2 = workroomsBase.appendingPathComponent(workroomName2, isDirectory: true)
566	    var dirs = [projectDir, workroomDir]
567	    // The on-disk dir keeps the short `workroomName` regardless (it's just a temp path); only the
568	    // MODEL's name — what the chip actually renders — swaps to the oversized value.
569	    var workrooms = [
570	      Workroom(
571	        name: longWorkroomName ? longWorkroomNameValue : workroomName, path: workroomDir.path,
572	        vcsName: vcs, warnings: [])
573	    ]
574	    if twoTabs {
575	      dirs.append(workroomDir2)
576	      workrooms.append(
577	        Workroom(name: workroomName2, path: workroomDir2.path, vcsName: vcs, warnings: []))
578	    }
579	    // Extra workrooms for the tab-bar overflow scenario (issue #129). `twoTabs` already contributes
580	    // `workroomName2`, so skip any name it seeded rather than listing a duplicate.
581	    for name in extraWorkroomNames where !workrooms.contains(where: { $0.name == name }) {
582	      let dir = workroomsBase.appendingPathComponent(name, isDirectory: true)
583	      dirs.append(dir)
584	      workrooms.append(Workroom(name: name, path: dir.path, vcsName: vcs, warnings: []))
585	    }
586	    for dir in dirs {
587	      try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: dir, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
588	    }
589	    // Seed one real working-tree file matching a `changedFiles` entry (`Gemfile`), so the in-app
590	    // "Open File" (issue #117) renders actual content instead of `PlainFileViewer`'s "File
591	    // unavailable" placeholder — `ChangesPanelUITests` asserts the marker below is on screen. Written
592	    // only if absent, so it stays idempotent within a launch.
593	    let seededGemfile = workroomDir.appendingPathComponent(seededFileName)
594	    if !FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: seededGemfile.path) {
595	      try? seededFileContent.write(to: seededGemfile, atomically: true, encoding: .utf8)
596	    }
597	    // Rewritten every launch, not written-if-absent: this content is an assertion fixture, so a stale
598	    // copy left in the temp dir by an older build must not silently outlive a change to it.
599	    let seededMarkdown = workroomDir.appendingPathComponent(seededMarkdownFileName)
600	    try? seededMarkdownContent.write(to: seededMarkdown, atomically: true, encoding: .utf8)
601	    return [Project(path: projectDir.path, vcs: vcs, workrooms: workrooms)]
602	  }

749	  /// A deterministic canned diff for the diff viewer in fixture mode — so the UI tests render a real
750	  /// `DiffViewer` without shelling out to git/jj against the fake temp directory. The content encodes
751	  /// the file path and the `DiffSource` (git worktree / jj `@` / jj `@-`) so a test can assert it
752	  /// opened the *right* file's diff from the *right* revision. Two paths get special states for
753	  /// coverage: `binary.bin` → binary, `clean.txt` → empty.
754	  ///
755	  /// Ruby files get a diff whose new-side lines are exactly `rubyFileContent(for:)` (a small Ruby
756	  /// snippet), so the real highlight pipeline (detect → parse → map) runs against canned content and
757	  /// the syntax-highlight UI test can assert colour was applied. The tag line is a Ruby comment, so
758	  /// the existing revision-tag assertions still hold. Non-Ruby paths keep a generic diff with no
759	  /// matching content, so they exercise the plain (highlight-skipped) fallback.
760	  static func diff(for descriptor: DiffDescriptor) -> DiffResult {
761	    let name = (descriptor.path as NSString).lastPathComponent
762	    if name == "binary.bin" { return .binary }
763	    if name == "clean.txt" { return .empty }
764	    if name == "huge.css" { return hugeDiff() }
765	    let tag = sourceTag(descriptor.source)
766	    if SyntaxLanguage.grammar(forPath: descriptor.path) == .ruby {
767	      return .diff(UnifiedDiff.parse(rubyDiffText(tag: tag, path: descriptor.path)))
768	    }
769	    let raw = """
770	      diff --git a/\(descriptor.path) b/\(descriptor.path)
771	      @@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
772	       context line one
773	      -removed old line
774	      +added line for \(tag)
775	      +marker \(descriptor.path)
776	       context line two
777	       context line three
778	      """
779	    return .diff(UnifiedDiff.parse(raw))
780	  }

782	  /// A large synthetic diff for the WORKROOM-2T hang-regression test (`DiffViewerLazyRenderingTests`):
783	  /// many separate hunks (not one giant hunk, to exercise the `ForEach`-in-`ForEach`-in-`List` nesting
784	  /// the real diff has) of long, no-whitespace-to-wrap-on lines — the minified-CSS shape that actually
785	  /// reproduced the App Hang. Defaults to exactly `UnifiedDiff.parse`'s 2000-line cap. Reached only via
786	  /// the `huge.css` magic path, so no other fixture path is affected.
787	  static func hugeDiff(hunkCount: Int = 20, linesPerHunk: Int = 100) -> DiffResult {
788	    var text = ""
789	    var newStart = 1
790	    for h in 0..<hunkCount {
791	      text += "@@ -0,0 +\(newStart),\(linesPerHunk) @@\n"
792	      for l in 0..<linesPerHunk {
793	        let n = h * linesPerHunk + l
794	        let hex = String(format: "%06x", n % 0xFF_FFFF)
795	        text +=
796	          "+.class-\(n){color:#\(hex);font-family:\"Barlow Condensed\",sans-serif;"
797	          + "src:url(/fonts/barlow-condensed-700.woff2) format(\"woff2\");"
798	          + "padding:0;margin:0;display:block;position:relative;z-index:1}\n"
799	      }
800	      newStart += linesPerHunk
801	    }
802	    return .diff(UnifiedDiff.parse(text))
803	  }

805	  /// Canned new-side file content for highlighting in fixture mode (mirrors `DiffResolver
806	  /// .fileContent`). Ruby files return a snippet whose lines match the Ruby diff above; everything
807	  /// else returns `nil` so it renders plain.
808	  static func fileContent(for descriptor: DiffDescriptor) -> String? {
809	    guard SyntaxLanguage.grammar(forPath: descriptor.path) == .ruby else { return nil }
810	    return rubyFileContent(tag: sourceTag(descriptor.source), path: descriptor.path)

813	  private static func sourceTag(_ source: DiffSource) -> String {
814	    switch source {

4	@testable import Workroom

6	/// The bundled libghostty runtime resources (`Resources/ghostty/terminfo` + `shell-integration`) are
7	/// a **coupled contract** with the engine's own Zig-side injection, and nothing at runtime validates
8	/// it: `GhosttyApp.resolveResources` only checks that the directory exists. When the pair drifts,
9	/// OSC 7 and OSC 133 degrade *silently* — no error, no log — taking ⌘-click path resolution, tab
10	/// titles and the busy indicator with them.
11	///
12	/// So `ghostty/CHECKSUMS` pins the bytes and this suite is the tripwire. It is the same shape as
13	/// `ThemeServiceTests.testBundledThemeChecksumsMatch`, for the same reason: a structural test cannot
14	/// see byte drift, because a drifted script still parses and still ships.
15	///
16	/// `themes/` is deliberately NOT covered here — it is ours, not upstream's, and carries its own
17	/// `themes/CHECKSUMS` with its own test.
18	final class GhosttyResourcesTests: XCTestCase {
19	  /// Read from `Bundle.main.resourceURL` rather than the source tree so this asserts on what
20	  /// actually ships — a resource dropped from the folder reference fails here, not silently at
21	  /// launch on a user's machine.
22	  private func resourceDir() throws -> String {
23	    try XCTUnwrap(
24	      Bundle.main.resourceURL?.appendingPathComponent("ghostty").path,
25	      "the app bundle must carry its ghostty resources — the terminal can't start without them")
26	  }
27	
28	  /// Every shipped file under `terminfo/` and `shell-integration/`, as paths relative to the
29	  /// `ghostty/` directory. `.DS_Store` is excluded because Finder can mint one in a folder
30	  /// reference at any time and it is not a resource.
31	  ///
32	  /// **Symlinks are a hard failure, not a skip.** `FileManager.enumerator(atPath:)` does not descend
33	  /// into a symlinked directory, and `fileExists` resolves the link — so classifying one as "a
34	  /// directory, skip it" would hide every file underneath from BOTH directions of the membership
35	  /// assertion, and the manifest would silently stop pinning what it claims to pin. That is not
36	  /// hypothetical here: upstream ships `terminfo/67/ghostty` as a symlink, so a regeneration done by
37	  /// copying a Ghostty.app tree reintroduces one. Dereference on copy (`cp -RL`); don't relax this.
38	  private func trackedRelativePaths() throws -> Set<String> {
39	    let root = try resourceDir()
40	    var found: Set<String> = []
41	    for subtree in ["terminfo", "shell-integration"] {
42	      let base = root + "/" + subtree
43	      let walker = FileManager.default.enumerator(atPath: base)
44	      while let entry = walker?.nextObject() as? String {
45	        let full = base + "/" + entry
46	        guard (entry as NSString).lastPathComponent != ".DS_Store" else { continue }
47	
48	        // lstat, so a link is seen as a link rather than as whatever it points at.
49	        let type =
50	          try FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: full)[.type] as? FileAttributeType
51	        if type == .typeSymbolicLink {
52	          XCTFail(
53	            "\(subtree)/\(entry) is a symlink — checksums can't pin it and a symlinked directory "
54	              + "would hide its contents from the manifest. Re-vendor with `cp -RL`.")
55	          continue
56	        }
57	        guard type == .typeRegular else { continue }
58	        found.insert(subtree + "/" + entry)
59	      }
60	    }
61	    return found
62	  }
63	
64	  /// The shipped bytes are the vetted bytes, for both the terminfo entries and every shell script.
65	  ///
66	  /// Membership is asserted in *both* directions on purpose. A checksum-only test passes when a file
67	  /// is deleted from the bundle, and a listing-only test passes when a file's contents change —
68	  /// which is precisely the drift this exists to catch.
69	  func testBundledResourceChecksumsMatch() throws {
70	    let dir = try resourceDir()
71	    let manifest = try XCTUnwrap(
72	      try? String(contentsOfFile: dir + "/CHECKSUMS", encoding: .utf8),
73	      "ghostty/CHECKSUMS must ship — it is what makes the vendored ref verifiable")
74	
75	    // Every non-blank line must parse, and every path must appear once. Skipping malformed lines
76	    // and last-write-wins on duplicates would both let a bad manifest pass: a merge artifact
77	    // carrying an obsolete AND a current checksum for one path would satisfy this test while
78	    // `shasum -c` rejected the file.
79	    var expected: [String: String] = [:]
80	    for line in manifest.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false) {
81	      let raw = String(line)
82	      guard !raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty else { continue }
83	      // `shasum -a 256` format: "<64 hex>  <path>" (two spaces; a path may itself contain spaces).
84	      let parts = raw.components(separatedBy: "  ")
85	      guard parts.count >= 2, parts[0].count == 64,
86	        parts[0].allSatisfy({ $0.isHexDigit })
87	      else {
88	        XCTFail("CHECKSUMS has a malformed line: \(raw)")
89	        continue
90	      }
91	      let path = parts.dropFirst().joined(separator: "  ")
92	      if expected[path] != nil {
93	        XCTFail("CHECKSUMS lists \(path) more than once — likely a merge artifact")
94	      }
95	      expected[path] = parts[0].lowercased()
96	    }
97	    XCTAssertFalse(expected.isEmpty, "CHECKSUMS parsed to nothing — wrong format?")
98	
99	    XCTAssertEqual(
100	      Set(expected.keys), try trackedRelativePaths(),
101	      "CHECKSUMS and the shipped terminfo / shell-integration files disagree on membership")
102	
103	    for (path, want) in expected {
104	      guard let data = FileManager.default.contents(atPath: dir + "/" + path) else {
105	        XCTFail("\(path): listed in CHECKSUMS but unreadable")
106	        continue
107	      }
108	      XCTAssertEqual(
109	        Self.sha256Hex(data), want,
110	        "\(path): contents differ from the vendored ghostty ref recorded in ghostty/SOURCE.md")
111	    }
112	  }
113	
114	  /// Nothing unexpected rides along inside the folder reference.
115	  ///
116	  /// `Resources/ghostty` is a **folder reference** in `project.yml`, so the whole directory is copied
117	  /// into the bundle verbatim and code-signing seals whatever is in it. Xcode's copy skips
118	  /// `.DS_Store`/`.git`/`.svn`/`.hg` and nothing else. That is a real hole rather than a theoretical
119	  /// one: agent-harness `.claude/.cc-writes` directories were found shipping inside the built app,
120	  /// and because they match a *global* gitignore they never appeared in `git status` — so neither
121	  /// the manifest (scoped to two subtrees) nor code review could see them.
122	  func testNoUnexpectedTopLevelResources() throws {
123	    let dir = try resourceDir()
124	    let allowed: Set<String> = [
125	      "terminfo", "shell-integration", "themes", "SOURCE.md", "CHECKSUMS",
126	    ]
127	    let present = Set(
128	      try FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(atPath: dir).filter { $0 != ".DS_Store" })
129	    XCTAssertEqual(
130	      present.subtracting(allowed), [],
131	      "unexpected entries in the ghostty folder reference — they ship inside the signed bundle")
132	  }
133	
134	  /// `themes/` must stay out of this manifest. It is ours, it changes on its own schedule, and it
135	  /// already has `themes/CHECKSUMS`. Folding it in here would make a theme refresh look like engine
136	  /// drift and vice versa — the two signals have to stay separable.
137	  func testChecksumsExcludesThemes() throws {
138	    let manifest = try XCTUnwrap(
139	      try? String(contentsOfFile: try resourceDir() + "/CHECKSUMS", encoding: .utf8))
140	    XCTAssertFalse(
141	      manifest.contains("themes/"),
142	      "themes/ is tracked by themes/CHECKSUMS — keep the two manifests disjoint")
143	  }
144	
145	  /// Both terminfo entries are the same compiled record under two names. Upstream ships the
146	  /// `ghostty` alias as a symlink; we ship a byte copy (see `ghostty/SOURCE.md`), so the two files
147	  /// can drift apart in our tree in a way they cannot in upstream's. Asserted so a regeneration that
148	  /// updates one and forgets the other is a test failure rather than a `TERM=ghostty` session
149	  /// quietly running on a stale entry.
150	  func testTerminfoAliasMatchesPrimaryEntry() throws {
151	    let dir = try resourceDir()
152	    let primary = FileManager.default.contents(atPath: dir + "/terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty")
153	    let alias = FileManager.default.contents(atPath: dir + "/terminfo/67/ghostty")
154	    XCTAssertNotNil(primary, "terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty must ship — line editing breaks without it")
155	    XCTAssertEqual(primary, alias, "the `ghostty` alias entry has drifted from `xterm-ghostty`")
156	  }
157	
158	  private static func sha256Hex(_ data: Data) -> String {
159	    SHA256.hash(data: data).map { String(format: "%02x", $0) }.joined()
160	  }

1	# Bundled libghostty runtime resources
2	
3	`GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR` points here at launch (see Core/GhosttyApp.swift). libghostty needs:
4	
5	- `terminfo/` — the `xterm-ghostty` / `ghostty` terminfo entries. libghostty sets
6	  `TERM=xterm-ghostty` for the shell but NOT `TERMINFO`, and macOS has no system entry for it, so
7	  `GhosttyApp` also exports `TERMINFO` → here (without it the shell can't resolve the terminal's
8	  capabilities and line editing — e.g. Backspace — breaks).
9	- `shell-integration/` — per-shell scripts Ghostty auto-injects; these report OSC 7 pwd
10	  (the cwd source for ⌘-click path resolution — see plan CMT-1) and more.
11	
12	- `themes/` — **ours, not upstream's.** 116 curated theme files whose names `ThemeService.families`
13	  parses — 114 vendored from iTerm2-Color-Schemes plus the two hand-authored `Workroom` themes,
14	  forming 58 dark/light families. Do NOT regenerate this directory from a ghostty checkout; it would
15	  break the theme picker. Its provenance is recorded separately in `themes/SOURCE.md` +
16	  `themes/CHECKSUMS`, and it is deliberately NOT covered by the `CHECKSUMS` file in this directory.
17	
18	## Provenance
19	
20	The `libghostty-spm` package ships no terminfo or shell-integration, so both are vendored here (once,
21	in `b81d5c6d`, the SwiftTerm → libghostty commit). This section records what was previously unknown.
22	`CHECKSUMS` in this directory pins the exact bytes of everything below, and
23	`GhosttyResourcesTests.testBundledResourceChecksumsMatch` recomputes and compares them.
24	
25	**Engine the measurements below were taken against:** whatever `macapp/project.yml` pinned on
26	2026-08-09 — read it, it is the single source of truth for the engine version and this file
27	deliberately does not duplicate it. The comparison baseline was a stock Ghostty.app install of that
28	same version. Re-measure after a pin bump; these findings expire with it.
29	
30	### `terminfo/` — matches the engine exactly
31	
32	Measured 2026-08-09: `terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty` is **byte-identical** to the same file in the stock
33	Ghostty.app install. `terminfo/67/ghostty` is the same compiled entry again under the `ghostty` alias
34	name (identical sha256), so a user's `TERM=ghostty` also resolves.
35	
36	Upstream ships that alias too, but as a **symlink** (`67/ghostty -> .././78/xterm-ghostty`); ours is
37	a byte copy. That difference is deliberate and load-bearing for `CHECKSUMS`: a regeneration done by
38	copying a Ghostty.app resource tree with `cp -R` reproduces the symlink, and `GhosttyResourcesTests`
39	**rejects symlinks** under the tracked subtrees rather than following them (a symlinked *directory*
40	would otherwise hide its whole contents from the manifest). If a regeneration trips that assertion,
41	dereference the links (`cp -RL`) rather than relaxing the test.
42	
43	Nothing to regenerate. Re-verify after an engine bump, not before.
44	
45	### `shell-integration/` — a main snapshot 12–52 days ahead of the engine
46	
47	Not from the v1.3.1 tag. `bash/ghostty.bash` is a byte-exact match for ghostty blob
48	`7eaf1397bdd9d04ae5ac5b85a0c9aa2ae392d902`, first reachable at `4b9324f4` (2026-03-20), and the zsh
49	script carries the trailing-`%` prompt fix from `43f3dc5f` (2026-03-25). Neither file changed again
50	until the `ghostty +ssh` migration on 2026-05-04/05, so the vendored set is consistent with **any
51	ghostty `main` commit in [`43f3dc5f` 2026-03-25 … `484d6ec6` 2026-05-04)** and cannot be narrowed
52	further from content alone.
53	
54	Being ahead of the engine is safe **here, on this pair**, and that was measured rather than assumed:
55	
56	- The injection contract is identical *between the two script sets*. Both reference exactly the same
57	  ten `GHOSTTY_*` variables (`GHOSTTY_BASH_ENV`, `_INJECT`, `_RCFILE`, `_UNEXPORT_HISTFILE`,
58	  `GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR`, `GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR`, `GHOSTTY_SAVE_PS`, `GHOSTTY_SHELL_FEATURES`,
59	  `GHOSTTY_SHELL_INTEGRATION_XDG_DIR`, `GHOSTTY_ZSH_ZDOTDIR`), so the drift introduced no new
60	  dependency. All ten are satisfied. We export `GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR` ourselves
61	  (`GhosttyResources.exportResourcesDir`, called from both `GhosttyApp` and `main.swift`); the engine
62	  sets the other nine itself, `GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR` among them — see the ssh section below, which
63	  corrects an earlier claim in this file that we left it unset.
64	- The OSC 133 vocabulary is a **strict subset**. Our scripts emit
65	  `133;A`/`B`/`C`/`D`/`P;k=i`/`P;k=s`; the engine's own scripts emit all of those plus `133;A;k=s`,
66	  which ours never send. So the pinned engine already parses every sequence we emit.
67	
68	What the drift buys is four upstream fixes v1.3.1 lacks: ble.sh cursor desync (`b1ad24e2`),
69	`PROMPT_COMMAND` ending in a newline (`1f3a3b41`), inherited-`PROMPT_COMMAND` "command not found" in
70	subshells (`4b9324f4`), and the trailing-`%` prompt corruption (`43f3dc5f`). **Do not "fix" this by
71	downgrading to the v1.3.1 scripts** — it would trade four real fixes for a version number.
72	
73	## The ssh wrapper, and the `ghostty` symlink that feeds it — RESOLVED
74	
75	Between our snapshot and any later ref, upstream **deleted the inline ssh wrapper** from every shell
76	script and replaced it with a call to `ghostty +ssh` (`484d6ec6` and follow-ups, 2026-05-04/05 —
77	"roughly a third of our shell integration scripts").
78	
79	**Two earlier claims in this file were wrong, and are corrected here.** It said we "never set
80	`GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR`", and concluded that either way out "has to set `GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR`". Neither holds:
81	
82	- **The engine sets it, and always has.** `src/termio/Exec.zig` does
83	  `env.put("GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR", dirname(executablePath()))` inside a block labelled `ghostty_path:`,
84	  and the literal is present in our own pinned archive among the other child-env strings (`TERMINFO`,
85	  `xterm-256color`, `GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR`, `MANPATH`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION`). For us it resolves to
86	  `Workroom.app/Contents/MacOS`. The variable was never unset — the directory just had no `ghostty`
87	  in it, so `"$GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR/ghostty" +ssh-cache` failed on a missing file rather than an empty
88	  path.
89	- **We did not need to build a CLI.** `libghostty` carries the entire `+action` implementation set:
90	  `src/build/GhosttyLib.zig` roots the library at `src/main_c.zig` → `global.zig` → `cli.zig`,
91	  unconditionally. Verified in our archive — `nm -gU` shows `_ghostty_init` and
92	  `_ghostty_cli_try_action`, `nm -a` shows `cli.ghostty.Action.runMain` and
93	  `cli.ssh-cache.DiskCache.*`, and `strings` carries the full `+ssh-cache` help text. Dispatch is a
94	  **two-call sequence**: `ghostty_init` parses and *stores* the action, `ghostty_cli_try_action` runs
95	  it and exits. The app called only the first, which is why nothing ever ran.
96	
97	**What ships now.** `Contents/MacOS/ghostty` is a **relative symlink to the app binary**, created by
98	the "Symlink ghostty" build phase in `project.yml` before Xcode's final code-sign, and `main.swift`
99	branches on `argv[0]` to run the CLI dispatch instead of starting the GUI. This is upstream's own
100	shape — `Ghostty.app/Contents/MacOS/ghostty` *is* the app binary there too — and it means the action
101	set we expose is exactly the pinned engine's, by construction: no second binary to keep in
102	architecture, signing or engine lockstep.
103	
104	Measured, not assumed (a throwaway bundle carrying the same symlink shape): `codesign` seals it
105	(`Sealed Resources … files=1`), and it survives `--verify --deep --strict`, a `ditto` zip round-trip,
106	notarization (`status: Accepted`), `stapler staple` + `validate`, a UDZO DMG round-trip, and
107	`spctl -a -vvv` (`accepted / source=Notarized Developer ID`) — still a symlink, still executing with
108	`argv[0] == "ghostty"`. `release.sh` asserts all of this on the real artifact, including actually
109	running `+ssh-cache` on it, because a build completing proves packaging, not function.
110	
111	**Consequence for the bump: regenerating `shell-integration/` is now safe** — but only *with or
112	after* the pin bump, never before it. `+ssh` does not exist at the pinned v1.3.1 (it is `main`-only,
113	in no tagged release) and arrives at the bump target `35e1a016`. Regenerating first would swap the
114	inline wrapper for a call to an action this engine does not have. TODOS.md's pin-bump entry carries
115	the blocking test that must accompany it.
116	
117	**Side effect worth knowing:** the engine puts `Contents/MacOS` on every pane's `PATH`, so inside a
118	Workroom terminal `ghostty` now resolves to this helper and shadows a real Ghostty.app. A bare
119	`ghostty` therefore prints a message naming Workroom and exits 1, rather than launching a second
120	copy of the app. `GhosttyCLITests` pins that behaviour.
121	
122	### Pre-bump latency baseline
123	
124	The wrapper calls `+ssh-cache` once per `ssh`. Measured on the Debug build (58 KB launcher + an
125	81 MB debug dylib — Release links statically and is faster), 20 runs each:
126	
127	| | per invocation |
128	|---|---|
129	| `ghostty +ssh-cache --host=…`, cold miss | ~21 ms |
130	| `ghostty +ssh-cache --host=…`, warm hit | ~21 ms |
131	| `infocmp -0 -x xterm-ghostty` (the fallback it replaces) | ~2.9 ms |
132	
133	Read it as: on a **miss** we pay ~21 ms of pure overhead and then take the `infocmp` path anyway; on
134	a **hit** those same ~21 ms replace `infocmp` *plus a full ControlMaster round-trip to the remote
135	host* to push terminfo, which is orders of magnitude more. Hosts are cached after first connect, so
136	steady state is hits and the cache is a clear win. Re-measure after the bump: `+ssh` moves the whole
137	wrapper into the binary, so this is the only before-picture we will have.
138	
139	## Why any of this is checked
140	
141	`GhosttyApp.resolveResources` only checks that the directory exists. The scripts and the engine's
142	Zig-side injection are a *coupled contract* (ZDOTDIR/ENV/XDG_DATA_DIRS, `GHOSTTY_SHELL_FEATURES`,
143	ssh integration) that nothing at runtime validates. If they drift apart, OSC 7 and OSC 133 degrade
144	**silently** — taking ⌘-click paths, tab titles and the busy indicator with them. There is no error
145	and no log; the terminal just quietly stops reporting things. `CHECKSUMS` plus its test is the only
146	tripwire.
147

**Engine the measurements below were taken against:** whatever `macapp/project.yml` pinned on
2026-08-09 — read it, it is the single source of truth for the engine version and this file
deliberately does not duplicate it. The comparison baseline was a stock Ghostty.app install of that
same version. Re-measure after a pin bump; these findings expire with it.

### `terminfo/` — matches the engine exactly

Measured 2026-08-09: `terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty` is **byte-identical** to the same file in the stock
Ghostty.app install. `terminfo/67/ghostty` is the same compiled entry again under the `ghostty` alias
name (identical sha256), so a user's `TERM=ghostty` also resolves.

Upstream ships that alias too, but as a **symlink** (`67/ghostty -> .././78/xterm-ghostty`); ours is
a byte copy. That difference is deliberate and load-bearing for `CHECKSUMS`: a regeneration done by
copying a Ghostty.app resource tree with `cp -R` reproduces the symlink, and `GhosttyResourcesTests`
**rejects symlinks** under the tracked subtrees rather than following them (a symlinked *directory*
would otherwise hide its whole contents from the manifest). If a regeneration trips that assertion,
dereference the links (`cp -RL`) rather than relaxing the test.

Nothing to regenerate. Re-verify after an engine bump, not before.

### `shell-integration/` — a main snapshot 12–52 days ahead of the engine

Not from the v1.3.1 tag. `bash/ghostty.bash` is a byte-exact match for ghostty blob
`7eaf1397bdd9d04ae5ac5b85a0c9aa2ae392d902`, first reachable at `4b9324f4` (2026-03-20), and the zsh
script carries the trailing-`%` prompt fix from `43f3dc5f` (2026-03-25). Neither file changed again
until the `ghostty +ssh` migration on 2026-05-04/05, so the vendored set is consistent with **any
ghostty `main` commit in [`43f3dc5f` 2026-03-25 … `484d6ec6` 2026-05-04)** and cannot be narrowed
further from content alone.

Being ahead of the engine is safe **here, on this pair**, and that was measured rather than assumed:

- The injection contract is identical *between the two script sets*. Both reference exactly the same
  ten `GHOSTTY_*` variables (`GHOSTTY_BASH_ENV`, `_INJECT`, `_RCFILE`, `_UNEXPORT_HISTFILE`,
  `GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR`, `GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR`, `GHOSTTY_SAVE_PS`, `GHOSTTY_SHELL_FEATURES`,
  `GHOSTTY_SHELL_INTEGRATION_XDG_DIR`, `GHOSTTY_ZSH_ZDOTDIR`), so the drift introduced no new
  dependency. All ten are satisfied. We export `GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR` ourselves
  (`GhosttyResources.exportResourcesDir`, called from both `GhosttyApp` and `main.swift`); the engine
  sets the other nine itself, `GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR` among them — see the ssh section below, which
  corrects an earlier claim in this file that we left it unset.
- The OSC 133 vocabulary is a **strict subset**. Our scripts emit
  `133;A`/`B`/`C`/`D`/`P;k=i`/`P;k=s`; the engine's own scripts emit all of those plus `133;A;k=s`,
  which ours never send. So the pinned engine already parses every sequence we emit.

What the drift buys is four upstream fixes v1.3.1 lacks: ble.sh cursor desync (`b1ad24e2`),
`PROMPT_COMMAND` ending in a newline (`1f3a3b41`), inherited-`PROMPT_COMMAND` "command not found" in
subshells (`4b9324f4`), and the trailing-`%` prompt corruption (`43f3dc5f`). **Do not "fix" this by
downgrading to the v1.3.1 scripts** — it would trade four real fixes for a version number.

### `terminfo/` — regenerated this bump: one capability changed

Previously measured byte-identical to a stock Ghostty.app install at the old pin (2026-08-09) — see

`src/terminfo/ghostty.zig` between `332b2aef` and `35e1a016` (checked directly against a fresh
checkout, not assumed) shows exactly one change: the `Se` (cursor-style-reset) capability's escape
sequence changed from `\E[2 q` (hard-reset to blinking block) to `\E[0 q` (reset to the user's
*configured default* cursor style) — every other capability is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Regenerated without a Zig build: `infocmp -x` decompiled the old bundled `terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty`
to source form, the one `Se=` line was hand-edited to match the upstream diff, and `tic -x` recompiled
it. `cmp` against the old binary confirms exactly one differing region; `infocmp -x` on the recompiled
binary, diffed source-to-source against the pre-edit dump, confirms no other capability moved. This is
a source-diff-driven edit, not a from-scratch decompile-then-guess — the next bump should do the same
(diff `src/terminfo/*.zig` at the two commits; if it's empty, terminfo needs no regeneration; if not,
translate the diff the same way rather than trusting a stock-install comparison, which needs a real
Zig build of the new engine to obtain).

byte-identical to `terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty` (same convention as before — see below).

copying a Ghostty.app resource tree with `cp -R` reproduces the symlink, and `GhosttyResourcesTests`
**rejects symlinks** under the tracked subtrees rather than following them (a symlinked *directory*
would otherwise hide its whole contents from the manifest). If a regeneration trips that assertion,
dereference the links (`cp -RL`) rather than relaxing the test. `tic` on this machine already
produces a real file for the alias, not a symlink, so this bump needed no extra dereferencing step
for terminfo specifically.

### `shell-integration/` — now copied straight from the pinned commit, not ahead of it

The previous vendoring (measured 2026-08-09) was a `main` snapshot 12–52 days ahead of the old pin,
carrying four fixes the old engine's tagged release lacked (see git history for the full account of
why that was safe). **That gap no longer exists.** This bump's target engine (`35e1a016`,
2026-07-09) is itself ~2 months past that old snapshot, so `shell-integration/` was regenerated by
copying directly from a fresh checkout at the exact pinned commit (`cp -RL src/shell-integration/.`,
dereferencing — upstream ships none as symlinks at this commit, confirmed) rather than carrying a
separate ahead-of-engine snapshot forward. The four previously-cited fixes (ble.sh cursor desync,

trailing-`%` prompt corruption) are all upstream of `35e1a016` and included by construction.

`zsh/.zshenv` are byte-unchanged; `bash/ghostty.bash`, `elvish/lib/ghostty-integration.elv`,

pin being safely behind a *newer* snapshot; now that both are the same commit, the two by construction
cannot disagree, so there is nothing left to re-verify there.
